author: hannah-whitall-smith
fields.title: The Christian’s Secret of a Happy Life
fields.description: Have you been longing to experience true happiness? The Christian Secret of a Happy Life is a transformative guide for Christians seeking lasting joy. If you struggle to surrender your worries and yearn for God’s guidance, this book is filled with practical insights and biblical wisdom to help you overcome doubt, find peace, and cultivate a deeper, more fulfilling relationship with God.

fields.title: God’s Side and Man’s Side
fields.body_html:
In discussing the life and walk of faith, I want to address a common misunderstanding that often hinders a clear understanding of the subject. This misunderstanding arises from the tendency to focus on only one aspect of the topic without considering the other. As a result, people often see a well-presented perspective on one side but overlook the balance that comes from viewing both sides together. Unsurprisingly, this can lead to a distorted view of the whole matter.

There are two strong, distinct sides to this subject and, like all other subjects, it cannot be fully understood unless both of these sides are kept constantly in view. I refer, of course, to God’s side and man’s side; or, in other words, to God’s part in the work of sanctification, and man’s part. These are very distinct and even contrasting. They are not contradictory. But, to a casual observer, they sometimes appear so.

This was illustrated to me in a striking manner not long ago. Two teachers of this higher Christian life held meetings in the same place, at alternate hours. One s poke only of God’s part in the work, and the other dwelt only upon man’s part. They were in perfect sympathy with one another. They knew they were each teaching different sides of the same great truth. A large part of their hearers also understood this. But, it was different with some of the hearers. One lady said, in great perplexity, “I cannot understand it at all.” Two preachers are trying to teach the same truth. Yet, they seem to contradict each other.”

I felt her puzzlement. It troubles many honest seekers of truth. Suppose two friends visit a famous building, then return home to describe it. One has seen only the north side, and the other only the south.

The first says, “They built the building in such a manner, and it has such and such stories and ornaments.” “Oh, no!” says the other, interrupting him. “You are quite mistaken. I saw the building.

They built it distinctly.

Its ornaments and stories were so and so.” A lively dispute would likely arise over their descriptions.

Then, the two friends would find they had described different sides of the building. Everyone would reconcile at once.

I want to be clear about the two sides in this matter. Focusing on one side, without seeing the other, will create false views of the truth. In brief, I would say that man's part is to trust and God's part is to work. These two roles are distinct, but they do not have to conflict with each other.

I mean this. Someone needs to do a certain work. God will deliver us from the power of sin and will make us perfect in every good work to do His will. “And we all, with unveiled face, beholding the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image from one degree of glory to another’s For this comes from the Lord who is the Spirit.”2 Corinthians 3:18. We must transform ourselves by renewing our minds. Then, we can prove God's good, acceptable, and perfect will. A real work is to be wrought in us and upon us. We must conquer besetting sins. We must overcome evil habits. We must root out wrong dispositions and feelings. We must develop holy tempers and emotions.

A positive transformation is to take place. So at least the Bible teaches. Now somebody must do this.

Either we must do it for ourselves, or another must do it for us. Most of us tried to do it ourselves at first, and failed. Then, we learned from the Scriptures and our own experience that we cannot do it.

But, the Lord Jesus Christ came to do it. He will do it for all who trust Him completely.

Now under these circumstances, what is the part of the believer, and what is the part of the Lord? The believer can only trust. The Lord, in whom he trusts, does the work entrusted to Him. Trusting and doing are opposite, and often contradictory. But, are they contradictory in this case? Manifestly not, because two different parties are concerned. It is a contradiction to say one party in a transaction trusted his case to another, but attended to it himself. But, when we say one party trusts the other in a transaction, and the other does it, we make a simple, harmonious statement.

We do not present a difficult problem. In this higher life, man's part is to trust, and God's is to do the thing entrusted to Him. The preacher, speaking for man, can only talk of surrender and trust. That is all a man can do. We all agree about this. Yet, such preachers are often criticized. Their words imply there is no other part. So, we only trust. And the cry goes out that this doctrine of faith does away with all realities. Souls are told to trust, and that's it. They then sit in a sort of religious easy-chair, dreaming away a life that has no real results.

This misapprehension arises, of course, from a failure to communicate. Either the preacher neglected to state, or the hearer failed to hear, the other side of the matter. It is, that when we trust, the Lord works. He does a great deal, not us. Our trust brings results. Our Lord undertakes what we trust to Him and accomplishes it. We do not act, but He does. This makes His work more effective.

The puzzle about the preaching of faith vanishes when this is clear. But critics target the preacher who favors God's view for a different reason. He does not speak of trust, for the Lord’s part is not to trust, but to work. The Lord does the thing entrusted to Him. He disciplines and trains the soul by inward exercises and outward providences.

He brings to bear all the resources of His wisdom and love upon the refining and purifying of that soul.

He makes all of a person's life and circumstances serve one purpose: to grow him in grace and to make him like Christ, hour by hour.

He carries him through a process of transformation, as his case requires. He makes actual and experimental the results for which the soul has trusted. We have dared, for instance, according to the c ommand in Romans. 6:11 “So you also must consider yourselves dead to sin and alive to God in Christ Jesus.” by faith to reckon ourselves dead unto sin. The Lord makes this real. He leads us to victory over self by His daily, providential discipline. Our reckoning is available only because God makes it real.

Yet, the preacher who focuses on this practical side is accused of having no faith. He is said to promote a gradual sanctification by works and to present an impossible task.

Now, sanctification is both a sudden step of faith and a gradual process of works. We consider it a step; God sees it as a process. By a step of faith, we get into Christ; by a process, we are made to grow up unto Him in all things.

By a step of faith, we trust the Divine Potter. By a gradual process, He makes us a vessel for His honor, fit for His use, and ready for every good work. To illustrate: I will describe, to a beginner, how to turn a lump of clay into a beautiful vessel. I first tell him the clay's role in the matter. All I can say is this: the potter puts the clay into his hands. It then lies passive, submitting to all his turning and overturning of it.

There is really nothing else to be said about the clay’s part. But could my hearer argue from this that nothing else is done, because I say that this is all the clay can do? If he is an intelligent hearer, he will not dream of doing so, but will say, “I understand. This is what the clay must do; but what must the potter do?” “Ah,” I answer, “now we come to the importan t part. The potter takes the abandoned clay and begins to work it. He molds it to his own will. He kneads and works it, he tears it apart and presses it together again, and he wets it and then suffers it to dry.

Sometimes he works at it for hours. Sometimes, he lays it aside for days and does not touch it. Then, when he has made it perfectly soft, he proceeds to make it into the vessel he has planned. He turns it on the wheel, planes, and smooths it. Then, he dries it in the sun. Next, he bakes it in the oven. Finally, he turns it out of his workshop, a vessel to his honor and fit for his use.” Will my hearer now say I am contradicting myself?

I had said the clay could do nothing but lie passive in the potter's hands. Now, I am demanding it to perform great work. To make itself into such a vessel is an impossible task. Surely not.

He will see that, while I spoke of the clay's part, I am now speaking of the potter's. These two are contrastive, but not contradictory. The clay must not do the potter's work, but yield to it. The harmony between these two teachings, which seem contradictory, is unmistakable. What can be said about man's role in this great work? He must surrender and trust without hesitation.

But, on God's side of the question, what can be said about the many, wondrous ways He accomplishes His work entrusted to Him? It is here that the growing comes in. The lump of clay would never grow into a beautiful vessel if it stayed in the clay-pit for thousands of years. But once is put into the hands of a skillful potter, and, under his fashioning, it grows rapidly into a vessel to his honor. So, the Heavenly Potter changes the abandoned soul. The Spirit changes it from glory to glory into the Lord's image.

You have taken a step of faith. You have put yourself completely in His hands. Now, you must expect Him to begin to work. His way of accomplishing what you entrusted to Him may differ from yours.

But he knows, and you must satisfy yourself. I knew a lady. She had entered this life of faith with a great outpouring of the Spirit and a wonderful flood of light and joy. She supposed, of course, this was a prep for some great service. She expected to be sent into the Lord's harvest field. Instead of this, her husband soon lost all his money. She shut herself in her house to do endless chores. This left her no time or strength for any gospel work.

She accepted the discipline. She then devoted herself to sweeping, dust, baking, and sewing. She would have done the same to preach, pray, or write for the Lord. Through this training, He made her a vessel “meet for the Master's use, and prepared unto every good work.” Another lady, who had come to faith under similar circumstances, expected to be sent to do some great work. Instead, she was shut up with two peevish invalid nieces to nurse, humor, and amuse them all day long.

Unlike the first lady, this one did not accept the training. She grew restless and angry. In the end, she rebelled. She lost all her blessings and fell into a state of cold misery. She had understood her part in trusting, at first. But, not knowing the divine way to do that, she took herself from the hands of the Heavenly Potter. The wheel marred the vessel.

I believe many a vessel has been similarly damaged due to a lack of understanding these things.

Christian experience matures over time. It is the work of God’s Holy Spirit. His power transforms us and helps us grow into Christ in all things. We can only reach this maturity by yielding ourselves to His mighty work. But, the Scriptures urge all believers to seek a present sanctification. It does not consist in the maturity of growth, but in the purity of heart. This may be as complete in the babe in Christ as in the veteran believer.

The lump of clay, once it comes under the potter's hand, is, at every hour of the process, just what the potter wants it to be. Therefore, it pleases him. But it is very far from maturing into the vessel he intends to make in the future. The baby may be perfect. It may please its mother. But, it is not what she wishes it to be when it matures.

The apple in June is a perfect apple for June. It is the best apple that June can produce. But, it is very different from the apple in October. That is a perfected apple. God's works are perfect at every stage of their growth. Man’s works are never perfect until they are in every respect complete. In this life of sanctification, we claim only this: By a step of faith, we put ourselves in the Lord's hands. We trust Him to work in us all His goodwill. By faith, we must keep ourselves there.

This is our part 8 in the matter. In doing so, we are, in the Scriptural sense, pleasing to God. It may require years of training to mature us into a vessel, fit for His honor and every good work. Our part is to trust; it is His to achieve the results. When we do our part, He never fails to do His, for no one ever trusted in the Lord and felt confounded.

Do not fear that if you trust or tell others to, it will end there. Trust is only the beginning and the foundation. When we trust, the Lord works. His work is an important part. And this explains that apparent paradox which puzzles so many. They say, “In one breath you tell us to do nothing but trust, and in the next you tell us to do impossible things. How can you reconcile such contradictory statements?”

We must reconcile them. It's like reconciling statements about a saw in a carpenter's shop. We say, at one moment, that the saw has cut a log. Then, we declare that the carpenter did it. The saw is the instrument used, the power that uses it is the carpenter’s. So, we yield ourselves to God. We also give our bodies to Him as instruments of righteousness. We find that He works in us to will and to do of His good pleasure. We can say with Paul, “I labored; yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me.”

For we are to be His workmanship, not our own. For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand, that we should walk in them . (Eph. 2:10.) Only God, who created us, can re-create us. He alone understands the “work of His own hands.” All attempts at self-creation mark the vessel. No soul can find its highest fulfillment except through His work. He “works all things after the counsel of His own will.”

I will, of course, focus on man's side in this matter. I am writing for men. I hope to teach believers how to fulfill their part of the great work. But I want it clearly understood. Unless I believed in God's work, I would not have written a word of this book.

fields.title: The Scripturalness of This Life
fields.body_html:
When I approach this subject of the true Christian life, that life which is hid with Christ in God, so many thoughts struggle for utterance that I am almost speechless. Where will I begin? What is the most important thing to say? How will I make people read and believe? The subject is so glorious, and human words seem so powerless! But something I am impelled to say. Someone must tell the secret.

For it is one of that victory which overcomes the world, that promised deliverance from all our enemies, for which every child of God longs and prays, but which seems so often and so generally to elude their grasp.

May God grant me to tell it so. I hope every believer who reads this book will see the truth in Jesus.

May they gain this glorious life for themselves. I am sure that every converted soul longs for victory and rest. Most feel, at times, that they are their birthright. Can you not remember, some of you, the shout of triumph your souls gave when you first became acquainted with the Lord Jesus, and had a glimpse of His mighty saving power? How sure you were of victory then! How easy it seemed, to be more than conquerors, through Him that loved you. Under the leadership of a Captain who had never been foiled in battle, how could you dream of defeat?

And yet, to many of you, how different has been your real experience. The victories have happened, but few and fleeting, the defeats many and disastrous. You have not lived as you feel children of God ought to live. There has been a resting in a clear understanding of truth, without pressing. After the power and life thereof. There has been a rejoicing in the knowledge of things testified of in the Scriptures, without a living realization of the things themselves, experienced in the soul. People believe in Christ, talk about Him, and serve Him, but they do not know him as the soul’s actual and very life, abiding there forever, and revealing Himself there continually in His beauty.

You have found Jesus as your Saviour and your Master, and you have tried to serve Him and advance the cause of His kingdom. You have studied the Holy Scriptures with great attention and have gathered much precious truth here from, which you have endeavored faithfully to practice, but despite all your knowledge and all your activities in the service of the Lord, your souls are starving in silence, and you cry out repeatedly for that bread and water of life which you saw promised in the Scriptures to all believers.

In the very depths of your hearts, you know that your experience is not a Scriptural experience; that, as an old writer says, your religion is “but a talk to what the early Christians enjoyed, possessed, and lived in.” And your souls have sunk within you, as day after day, and year after year, your early visions of triumph have seemed to grow more and more dim, and you have forced yourself to settle down to the conviction that the best you can expect from your religion is a life of alternate failure and victory; one hour sinning, and the next repenting; and beginning again, only to fail again, and again to repent.

Is this all? Had the Lord Jesus only this in His mind when He laid down His precious life to deliver you from your sore and cruel bondage to sin? Did he propose to himself only this partial deliverance?

Did he intend to leave you thus struggling along under a weary consciousness of defeat and discouragement? Did He fear that a continuous victory would dishonor Him and bring reproach on His name?

When He made those declarations about His coming and the work He was to do. Did they mean only what you have experienced? Was there a hidden reserve in each promise that was meant to deprive it of its complete fulfillment? Did each promise contain a reserve that aimed to deprive it of its complete fulfillment? Did “delivering us out of the hands of our enemies” mean only a few of them? Did “enabling us always to triumph” mean only sometimes , or did being “more than conquerors through Him that love us” mean constant defeat and failure?

No, no, a thousand times no! God can save unto the uttermost, and He means to do it. His promise, confirmed by His oath, was that “He would grant unto us, that we, being delivered out of the hand of our enemies, might serve Him without fear, in holiness and righteousness before Him, all the days of our life.” It is a mighty work to do, but our Deliverer can do it. He came to destroy the works of the devil, and dare we dream for a moment that He is not able or not willing to do His own purposes?

In the very outset, then, settle down on this one thing, that the Lord can save you completely, now, in this life, from the power and dominion of sin, and to deliver you altogether out of the hands of your enemies. If you do not think He is, search your Bible, and collect together every announcement or declaration about the purposes and object of His death on the cross. You will be astonished to see how full they look.

Everywhere and always, His work is said to be to deliver us from our sins, from our bondage, from our defilement; and not a hint is given anywhere that this deliverance was to be only the limited and partial one with which the Church so continually tries to be satisfied.

Let me give you a few texts on this subject. Where will I begin? What is the most important thing to say? How will I make people read and believe? The subject is so glorious, and human words seem so powerless! But something I am impelled to say. Someone must tell the secret. For it is one of that victory which overcomes the world, that promised deliverance from all our enemies, for which every child of God longs and prays, but which seems so often and so generally to elude their grasp. May God grant me to tell it so. I hope every believer who reads this book will see the truth in Jesus. May they gain this glorious life for themselves. I am sure that every converted soul longs for victory and rest. Most feel, at times, that they are their birthright. Under the leadership of a Captain who had never been foiled in battle, how could you dream of defeat? And yet, to many of you, how different has been your real experience. The victories have happened, but few and fleeting, the defeats many and disastrous. You have not lived as you feel children of God ought to live. There has been a resting in a clear understanding of truth, without pressing. After the power and life thereof. There has been a rejoicing in the knowledge of things testified of in the Scriptures, without a living realization of the things themselves, experienced in the soul. People believe in Christ, talk about Him, and serve Him, but they do not know him as the soul’s actual and very life, abiding there forever, and revealing Himself there continually in His beauty. You have found Jesus as your Saviour and your Master, and you have tried to serve Him and advance the cause of His kingdom. You have studied the Holy Scriptures with great attention and have gathered much precious truth here from, which you have endeavored faithfully to practice, but despite all your knowledge and all your activities in the service of the Lord, your souls are starving in silence, and you cry out repeatedly for that bread and water of life which you saw promised in the Scriptures to all believers. fields.title: The Life Defined
fields.body_html:
In my last chapter, I tried to settle the question of the scripturalness of the Higher Christian Life. I best describe it as the “life hidden with Christ in God.” I now, therefore, consider it settled. The Scriptures promise Jesus' believers a life of perfect rest. It will be a constant victory, beyond normal Christian experience. They present a Saviour who can save us from the power of our sins, just as He saves us from their guilt.

The next point to consider is, what this hidden life is. How does it differ from other Christian experiences? It means letting the Lord manage our affairs and carry our burdens, instead of trying to do it all ourselves. Most Christians are like a man, toiling along the road under a heavy burden. A wagon overtook him, and the driver kindly offered to help him. He accepted the offer with great enthusiasm. But, when seated, his burden weighed him down. He still had it on his shoulders. “Why don’t you lay down your burden?” asked the kind - hearted driver. “Oh!” replied the man, “I feel that it is almost too much to ask you to carry me, and I could not think of letting you carry my burden too.”

Christians, who have entrusted themselves to the Lord Jesus, still bear their burdens. They often grow weary and heavy-laden on their journey. By “burdens,” I mean anything that troubles us, whether spiritual or temporal.

I mean, first of all, ourselves. The greatest burden we have to carry in life is self. The most difficult thing we have to manage is self. Our daily lives, feelings, and unique flaws and desires trouble us most.

They often lead us into bondage and darkness.

In laying off your burdens, so, the first one you must get rid of is yourself. You must hand over to God your inner self. This includes your temptations, temperament, and feelings. Then, leave them there. He made you, and so He understands you and knows how to manage you, and you must trust Him to do it.

Say to Him, “Here, Lord, I abandon myself to you. I have tried in every way I could think of to manage myself and to make myself what I know I ought to be, but have always failed.

Now I give it up to you. Do take entire possession of me. Work in me all the good pleasure of your will. Mould and fashion me into such a vessel as seems good to you. I leave myself in your hands. I believe you will, as you promised, make me a vessel for your honor. “Sanctified, and fit for the Master's use, and prepared for every good work.” Now, you must rest, trusting Him completely. Next, you must lay off every other burden. Your health, reputation, Christian work, houses, children, business, and servants. Everything that concerns you, inward or outward.

Christians always commit their souls to the Lord for eternity. They know, without a doubt, that they cannot keep themselves. But, they take the things of this life into their own keeping. They try to carry them with an unconfessed feeling. It is a lot to ask the Lord to carry them, and they cannot think to ask Him to carry their burdens too.

I knew a Christian lady who had a very heavy temporal burden. It took away her sleep and her appetite, and there was danger of her health breaking down under it. One day, it felt especially heavy. She noticed a little tract called “Hannah's Faith” on the table near her.” Attracted by the title, she picked it up and began to read. She did not know it would revolutionize her whole experience. The story was about a poor woman who had endured great sorrow.

Once, she told a kind visitor the history of her life. At the end, the visitor said, “O, Hannah, I cannot see how you could bear so much sorrow!” “I did not bear it,” was the quick reply. “The Lord bore it for me.” “Yes,” said the visitor. “That is the right way.” “You must take your troubles to the Lord.”

“Yes,” replied Hannah. “But, we must do more; we must leave them there. Most people,” she continued, “take their burdens to Him, but they bring them back. They're as worried and unhappy as ever.” But I take mine, and I leave them with Him, and come away and forget them. And if the worry returns, I take it to Him again. I do this over and over, until I forget my worries and am at perfect rest.”

My friend was very much struck with this plan and resolved to try it. She could not change her life. So, she took it to the Lord. She handed it over to Him. Then, she believed He took it. She left all her worries and anxieties with Him. Her anxieties returned often. She took them back. So, though things remained unchanged, her soul found perfect peace. She felt she had found a blessed secret. From then on, she tried never again to carry her own burdens or manage anything for herself. The secret worked wonders in her outer affairs. It was even more effective in her inner ones, which were even more unmanageable.

She gave her whole self to the Lord. She trusted Him with all she had. So, she stopped worrying. Her life became happy, for she belonged to Him. And this was the Higher Christian Life! It was a very simple secret she found out.

Only this. One could obey God's commandment in these words: “ Do not be anxious about anything, but in everything by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known to God. “Philippians 4 :6. If one obeyed, the result would be, according to the promise, that the “peace of God, which passes all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.” There is more to say about this life hid with Christ in God. Many details exist about what the Lord Jesus does for those who abandon themselves to Him. The gist of the matter is here. The soul that knows this secret has a key.

It will unlock God's treasure-house. I hope I have made you long for this blessed life.

Would you not like to get rid of your burdens? Do you not long to hand over the management of your unmanageable self into the hands of one who can manage you? Are you not tired? Does the rest I speak of not look sweet to you? Do you recall the blissful rest you felt after a tiring day, before bed? How delightful it was to relax every muscle. To let my body go in perfect ease and comfort. The strain of the day had ceased for a few hours at least, and the workers had thrown off the work of the day. You no longer had to hold up an aching head or a weary back. You trusted the bed completely. It held you up without any struggle. You rested. But suppose you had doubted your bed's strength. And, you feared it would give way and drop you to the floor. Could you have rested then? Wouldn't every muscle have strained to hold yourself up? Wouldn't the weariness have been greater than not to have gone to bed at all?

Let this analogy teach you what it means to rest in the Lord. Let your souls lie down upon His sweet will, as your bodies lie down in your beds at night. Relax every strain and lay off every burden.

Abandon all ease and comfort. Trust that, when He holds you up, you are safe. Your only task is to rest. His part is to sustain you, and He cannot fail. Or, take another analogy, which our Lord has sanctioned: that of the child-life said, “And calling to him a child, he put him in the midst of them and said, 'Truly, I say to you, unless you turn and become like children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.” Mathew 18:2 -3 Now, what are the characteristics of a little child, and how does he live? He lives by faith, and his primary characteristic is thoughtlessness. His life is one long trust from year’s end to year’s end. He trusts his parents, caretakers, and teachers. He even trusts some unworthy people, due to his confiding nature. And his trust receives a generous response. He provides nothing for himself, and yet he receives everything. He makes no plans for tomorrow. Yet, he plans his life. His paths open up to him as he reaches them, hour by hour, day by day. He enters and leaves his father's house with ease and freedom.

He enjoys its treasures, having spent nothing to get them.

Plague may walk through the streets of his city, but he regards it not. Famine, fire, and war may rage around him. But, under his father's care, he rests in perfect peace. He lives in the present, accepting life as it comes. I once visited a wealthy house with an adopted only child. He received all the love and care that human hearts and means could provide. Watching that child run in and out, day by day, I saw a picture of our wonderful position as children in our Father's house. The child was free and light-hearted, with the happy carelessness of childhood.

I thought, “If nothing could grieve her loved ones, it would be to see this child worry about herself.”

How much more must our God's loving heart grieve at His children's worries? I understood the reason our Lord had emphasized, “Take no thought for yourselves.” Who is best cared for in every household?

Is it not the little children? And does not the least of all, the helpless baby, receive the largest share? A late writer said that the baby “toils not, neither does he spin; nor yet someone feeds him, clothes him, loves him, and rejoices in him.” No one rejoices in him more than he does.

This life of faith, then, about which I am writing, consists in this: being a child in the Father’s house.

When someone says this, they say enough. It can transform every weary, burdened life into one of blessedness and rest.

Let the carefree confidence of your little ones teach you how to be with God. It pleases you and wins your hearts. Leave yourselves in His hands. “Do not be anxious about anything, but in everything by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known to God. And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.”

Philipians4:6-7 Notice the word 'nothing' in the above passage. It covers all possible grounds for anxiety, both inward and outward. We often feel pressured to believe it is our duty to be anxious about certain matters.

We will think, “it's right to give up all anxiety. In spiritual matters, anxiety is wrong. But we must be anxious about some things. It would be a sin not to be. We must worry about our children, those we love, our church, the truth, and our business.” It would show a great want of right feeling not to be anxious about such things as these.” Or, we may think, “Ye s, it's right to trust the Lord with our loved ones and affairs. But we should worry about our inner lives, our faith, our temptations, and our sins. If we don't, they will neglect them.”

We find the answer to such suggestions, and to all similar ones, in our text: “Therefore I tell you, do not be anxious about your life, what you will eat or what you will drink, nor about your body, what you will put on. Isn't life more than food, and the body more than clothing?

Look at the birds of the air: they neither sow nor reap nor gather into barns, and yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not of more value than they? And which of you by being anxious can add a single hour to his span of life? And why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow: they neither toil nor spin, yet I tell you, even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these. But if God so clothes the grass of the field, which today is alive and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, will he not much more clothe you, O you of little faith? Therefore do not be anxious, saying, ‘What shall we eat?’ or ‘What shall we drink?’ or ‘what shall we wear?’’ Mathew 6:25-31 “For the Gentiles seek after all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them all.

But seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to you.

“Therefore do not be anxious about tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Sufficient for the day is its own trouble.” I n Matt. 6:32-34, our Lord illustrates this being without anxiety, by telling us to behold the fowls of the air and the lilies of the field, as examples of the sort of life He would have us live. We must, without anxiety or fear, be like the birds and lilies. The birds rejoice in God's care and receive food. The lilies grow in His sunlight. Let the sparrows speak to us: “I am a tiny sparrow, a bird of low degree. My life is of little value, but the dear Lord cares for me. I have no barn nor storehouse. I neither sow nor reap. He gives me a sparrow's portion, but never a seed to keep. “I know there are many sparrows. People find them all over the world. But our heavenly Father knows when one of us falls to the ground. “Though small, we are never forgotten. Though weak, we are never afraid. For we know the dear Lord keeps the life of the creatures he made. “I soar above the densest trees and settle on many branches.” I have no chart nor compass, but I never lose my way.”

I fold my wing at twilight, wherever I may be. The Father is always watching. No harm will come to me. I am only a little sparrow, a bird of low degree. But I know the Father loves me. Have you less faith than we?”

fields.title: How to Enter In
fields.body_html:
I have tried to settle the question of the scripturalness of the experience of this life of full trust. I have also shown a little of what it is. The next point is how to reach and realize it. And first, I would say that we must not look upon this blessed life in any sense as an attainment but as an obtainment. We cannot earn it, we cannot climb up to it, we cannot win it; we can do nothing but ask for it and receive it. It is the gift of God in Christ Jesus. And where a thing is a gift, the only course left for the receiver is to take it and thank the giver. We never say of a gift, “See what I have attained,” and boast of our skill in gaining it. Instead, we say, “See what the giver has given me,” and we boast of the giver's love and generosity.

And everything in our salvation is a gift. From beginning to end, God is the giver and we are the receivers. The richest promises are not for those who do great things. They are for those who “receive plenty of grace, and of the gift of righteousness.” To know this inner life, the soul must be receptive. It must recognize completely that it is to be God's gift in Christ Jesus. We cannot gain it through any efforts or works of our own. This will make things much simpler. The only question left is who will receive this gift from God, and how to accept it. I would answer that He grants it only to the soul that is completely consecrated. You must receive it by faith.

Consecration is the first thing. Not in any legal sense, nor to buy or deserve it. But, to remove the obstacles and allow God to give it. To create a beautiful vessel from a lump of clay, the potter must have complete control over it. It must lie passive in his hands. To make a soul a vessel for God's honor, it must be “sanctified and meet for the Master's use, and prepared unto every good work.” It must be completely abandoned to Him and remain passive in His hands. This is manifest at the first glance.

I once tried to explain to a hospital doctor the meaning and need for consecration. But, he seemed unable to understand. At last, I said to him, “Suppose, in your rounds, you meet a man who begs you to cure him. But, he won't tell you all his symptoms or take your remedies.

He'd say, 'I'm willing to follow your directions on some things, as they seem good to me. But, in other matters, I prefer to follow my own judgment.' What would you do?” I asked.

“Do!” he replied with indignation, “do! I would soon leave such a man as that to his own care. “Of course,” he added. “I could do nothing for him. He must obey my directions.” “So, patients must obey doctors to be cured?” “Implicitly obeyed!” was his emphatic reply. “And that is 20 consecration,” I continued. “God must have the whole case, without reserves. His directions must be followed implicitly.” “I see it,” he exclaimed, -- “I see it! And I will do it. God must have His own way with me from henceforth.”

Some may think “abandonment” is a better word. But whatever we use, we mean a total surrender to God. We give Him our spirit, soul, and body. We want Him to do with us as He pleases. We mean that our soul's language in all things should express, “Your will be done. “We mean giving up all choice.

We mean a life of inevitable obedience. To a soul ignorant of God, this may look hard. But to those who know Him, it is the happiest and most restful of lives. He is our Father. He loves us and knows what is best. So, His will is the most blessed thing that can come to us, no matter the circumstances. I do not understand how it is that Satan has succeeded in blinding the eyes of the Church to this fact. But it seems God's children fear His will more than anything. His lovely, lovable will means only good for their souls. It brings loving-kindness, tender mercies, and great blessings.

I wish I could only show everyone the unfathomable sweetness of the will of God. Heaven is a place of infinite bliss. His will is perfectly done there. Our lives share in this bliss as His will is done in them.

He loves us, loves us, and the will of love is always a blessing for its loved one. Some of us know love.

If we could, we would bless our beloved ones. We would shower them with all that is good and lovely in life if we had the power to fulfill our wish for them.

And if this is the way of love with us, how much more must it be so with our God, who is love itself.

If we could see, even for a moment, the depths of His love, we would rush to embrace His will as our greatest treasure. We would abandon ourselves to it, filled with joy and gratitude for such a privilege.

Many Christians believe their Father in heaven wants to make them miserable and take their blessings.

They imagine, poor souls, that if they cling to their own will, they can stop Him from doing this. I am ashamed to write the words, and yet we must face a fact which is making wretched hundreds of lives.

A Christian lady, feeling this way, told a friend how hard it was to say, “Your will be done,” and how afraid she was to do it. She was the mother of one only little boy, who was the heir to a great fortune, and the idol of her heart. After she shared her troubles, her friend said, “What if your little Charley runs to you tomorrow?” He says, 'Mother, I have decided to let you have your way with me from now on.'

I'm always going to obey you. “I want you to do what you think is best with me.”

I know you love me, and I will trust your love. How would you feel towards him? Would you say to yourself, ‘Ah, now I shall have a chance to make Charley miserable?

I will take away all his pleasures, and fill his life with every hard and disagreeable thing I can find. I will force him to do the hardest things. Then, I w ill give him all sorts of impossible commands.” “Oh, no, no, no!” exclaimed the indignant mother. “You know I would not. I would hug him to my heart and cover him with kisses. I would fill his life with the sweetest, best things.” “And are you more tender and more loving than God?” asked her friend. “Ah, no,” was the reply. “I see my mistake. I will not fear saying 'Your will be done,' to my Heavenly Father, any more than I'd want my Charley to fear saying it to me.””

Better and sweeter than health, or friends, or money, or fame, or ease, or prosperity, is the adorable will of our God. It brightens the dark hours with a divine halo. It sheds bright sunshine on the gloomiest paths. He always reigns who has made it his kingdom; and nothing can go amiss to him. A glorious privilege is opening before you. The first step to enter the life hidden with Christ in God is complete consecration. I cannot have you look at it as a hard and stern demand. You must do it with joy, appreciation, and enthusiasm. You must enter what I call the privilege side of consecration. I assure you, from a blessed experience, it is the happiest place you will ever find.

Faith is the next thing. Faith is essential to receiving any gift. Our friends may give us something in its entirety, but we do not own it until we believe they have given it and we claim it. This is especially true for gifts that are purely mental or spiritual. Another may love us without limit. But, until we believe it, it never becomes ours. I suppose most Christians know this about their forgiveness.

They know that the preaching of Jesus' forgiveness of sins might have gone on forever. But, it would never be theirs until they claimed the forgiveness. They had to believe it first. But, in living the Christian life, they lose sight of this. They think, having been saved by faith, they must now live by works. Instead of continuing to receive, they now must begin to do. This makes our declaration that the life hid with Christ in God is to be entered by faith, seem perfectly unintelligible to them.

And yet it is plainly declared, that “as we have received Christ Jesus the Lord, so we are to walk in Him.” We received Him by faith, and by faith alone; so we are to walk in Him by faith, and by faith alone. Our faith in this hidden life is the same as the faith that moved us from the kingdom of darkness to God's Son. It just relies on a different thing. Then we believed that Jesus was our Saviour from sin's guilt. Our faith made it so. Now, we must believe He is our Saviour from sin's power. Our faith will make it so. We trusted Him for our justification, and it became ours. Now, we must trust Him for our sanctification, and it shall be ours, too. Then we took Him as a Saviour in the future from our sins' penalties. Now, we must take Him as a Saviour in the present from our sins' bondage.

Then He was our Redeemer, now He is to be our Life. Then He lifted us from the pit. Now, He is to seat us in heavenly places with Himself. I mean this based on both experimental and practical evidence.

I know, theologically and judicially, that every believer has everything at conversion. But experimentally, nothing is his until by faith he claims it. “ Every place that the sole of your foot will tread upon me have given to you, just as I promised to Moses. “Joshua 1:3. “Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places,”Ephesians1:3. But, until we have faith in them, they are not ours. “According to our faith,” is always the limit and the rule.

But this faith of which I am speaking must be a present faith. No faith that people exercise in the future tense amounts to anything. A man may believe forever that some future time will forgive his sins, and he will never find peace. He has to come to the now belief, and say by faith, “My sins are now forgiven,” before he can live the new life. Also, no faith that seeks future rescue from sin will lead a soul into the life we describe. The enemy delights in this future faith. He knows it is powerless to achieve any results.

But he trembles and flees when a believer claims to be free from his power. In short: to enter this blessed life of rest and triumph, you must take two steps. First, abandon all.

Second, have absolute faith.

Whatever your troubles, these two steps will help you. If you take them, and stick to them, they will lead you to a better Christian life. You may be sure of this. If you will set aside all else, and focus on these two points, your progress will be swift. You will reach your soul's desired haven sooner than you now think possible.

Must I repeat the steps, that there may be no mistake? You are a child of God, and long to please Him.

You love your precious Saviour, and are sick and weary of the sin that grieves Him. You long for someone to deliver you from its power. All you've tried has failed. In despair, you now wonder if, as these happy people say, the Lord can and will save you. You know in your soul that He can. To save you from all your enemies is His purpose.

Then trust Him. Commit your case to Him. Abandon all else and believe He will take it. Knowing what He is and what He has said, claim that He provides complete salvation for you now. At first, you believed He freed you from sin's guilt because He said so. Now, believe that He frees you from sin's power because He says so. Let your faith now lay hold of a new power in Christ. You have trusted Him as your dying Saviour, now trust Him as your living Saviour. Just as much as He came to deliver you from future punishment, didn’t He also come to deliver you from present bondage. As He came to bear your sins for you, He has come to live His life within you.

You are completely powerless in both cases. You could rid yourself of your own sins with the same effort. As you could now achieve practical righteousness. Christ, and Christ only, must do both for you.

Your part is to give the thing to Him, and then believe He does it.

A now eminent lady, in a great darkness, sought to enter in. She said to a friend trying to help her, “You all say, 'Abandon yourself, and trust.' But I do not know how.” I wish you would just do it out loud, so that I may see how you do it.”Must I do it out loud for you?

“Lord Jesus, You can and will deliver me from all the cares and troubles of my Christian life. You died to set me free, not in the future, but now and here.” you are stronger than Satan. You can keep me, even in my weakness, from falling into his traps or obeying him. And, Lord, I am going to trust thee to keep me. I have tried to maintain my composure, and I have failed, suffering a significant setback. I am completely helpless; so, I will trust you now. I will give myself to thee; I hold nothing back. Body, soul, and spirit, I present myself, a worthless lump of clay. Make me into whatever thy love and wisdom choose. And now, I am thine.

You accept what I present. Your power has taken my weak, foolish heart. You have begun to work in me to will and to do of your good pleasure. I trust you completely, and I trust you now! Are you afraid to take this step? Does it seem too sudden, too much like a leap in the dark? Do you not know that the steps of faith always “fall on the seeming void, but find the rock beneath”? A man, having to descen d a well by a rope, found, to his horror, when he was a great way down, that it was too short. He had reached the end, and yet was, he estimated, about thirty feet from the bottom of the well. He knew not what to do. He lacked the strength or skill to climb up the rope, and letting go would dash him to pieces.

His arms began to fail. He decided to let go and meet his fate. He resigned himself to destruction, and loosened his grasp. He fell! To the bottom of the well it was -- three inches! If ever your feet are to touch the “rock beneath,” you must let go of every hold and drop into God. For, there is no other way.

And to do it now may save you months and even years of strain and weariness. In all the old castles of England there used to be a place called the keep. It was the castle's strongest, best-protected place. It hid the weak and helpless in times of danger. If you were a timid, helpless woman in a castle under siege, would you have dared to hide there?

Would you have been afraid to do it? Must we fear to hide in the keeping power of our Divine Keeper?

He neither slumbers nor sleeps. He has promised to preserve our going out and coming in, now and forever.
fields.body_text: I have tried to settle the question of the scripturalness of the experience of this life of full trust. I have also shown a little of what it is. The next point is how to reach and realize it. And first, I would say that we must not look upon this blessed life in any sense as an attainment but as an obtainment. We cannot earn it, we cannot climb up to it, we cannot win it; we can do nothing but ask for it and receive it. It is the gift of God in Christ Jesus. And where a thing is a gift, the only course left for the receiver is to take it and thank the giver. We never say of a gift, “See what I have attained,” and boast of our skill in gaining it. Instead, we say, “See what the giver has given me,” and we boast of the giver's love and generosity. And everything in our salvation is a gift. From beginning to end, God is the giver and we are the receivers. The richest promises are not for those who do great things. They are for those who “receive plenty of grace, and of the gift of righteousness.” To know this inner life, the soul must be receptive. It must recognize completely that it is to be God's gift in Christ Jesus. We cannot gain it through any efforts or works of our own. This will make things much simpler. The only question left is who will receive this gift from God, and how to accept it. I would answer that He grants it only to the soul that is completely consecrated. You must receive it by faith. Consecration is the first thing. Not in any legal sense, nor to buy or deserve it. But, to remove the obstacles and allow God to give it. To create a beautiful vessel from a lump of clay, the potter must have complete control over it. It must lie passive in his hands. To make a soul a vessel for God's honor, it must be “sanctified and meet for the Master's use, and prepared unto every good work.” It must be completely abandoned to Him and remain passive in His hands. This is manifest at the first glance. I once tried to explain to a hospital doctor the meaning and need for consecration. But, he seemed unable to understand. At last, I said to him, “Suppose, in your rounds, you meet a man who begs you to cure him. But, he won't tell you all his symptoms or take your remedies. He'd say, 'I'm willing to follow your directions on some things, as they seem good to me. But, in other matters, I prefer to follow my own judgment.' What would you do?” I asked. “Do!” he replied with indignation, “do! I would soon leave such a man as that to his own care. “Of course,” he added. “I could do nothing for him. He must obey my directions.” “So, patients must obey doctors to be cured?” “Implicitly obeyed!” was his emphatic reply. “And that is 20 consecration,” I continued. “God must have the whole case, without reserves. His directions must be followed implicitly.” “I see it,” he exclaimed, -- “I see it! And I will do it. God must have His own way with me from henceforth.” Some may think “abandonment” is a better word. But whatever we use, we mean a total surrender to God. We give Him our spirit, soul, and body. We want Him to do with us as He pleases. We mean that our soul's language in all things should express, “Your will be done. “We mean giving up all choice. We mean a life of inevitable obedience. To a soul ignorant of God, this may look hard. But to those who know Him, it is the happiest and most restful of lives. He is our Father. He loves us and knows what is best. So, His will is the most blessed thing that can come to us, no matter the circumstances. I do not understand how it is that Satan has succeeded in blinding the eyes of the Church to this fact. But it seems God's children fear His will more than anything. His lovely, lovable will means only good for their souls. It brings loving-kindness, tender mercies, and great blessings. I wish I could only show everyone the unfathomable sweetness of the will of God. Heaven is a place of infinite bliss. His will is perfectly done there. Our lives share in this bliss as His will is done in them. He loves us, loves us, and the will of love is always a blessing for its loved one. Some of us know love. If we could, we would bless our beloved ones. We would shower them with all that is good and lovely in life if we had the power to fulfill our wish for them. And if this is the way of love with us, how much more must it be so with our God, who is love itself. If we could see, even for a moment, the depths of His love, we would rush to embrace His will as our greatest treasure. We would abandon ourselves to it, filled with joy and gratitude for such a privilege. Many Christians believe their Father in heaven wants to make them miserable and take their blessings. They imagine, poor souls, that if they cling to their own will, they can stop Him from doing this. I am ashamed to write the words, and yet we must face a fact which is making wretched hundreds of lives. A Christian lady, feeling this way, told a friend how hard it was to say, “Your will be done,” and how afraid she was to do it. She was the mother of one only little boy, who was the heir to a great fortune, and the idol of her heart. After she shared her troubles, her friend said, “What if your little Charley runs to you tomorrow?” He says, 'Mother, I have decided to let you have your way with me from now on.' I'm always going to obey you. “I want you to do what you think is best with me.” I know you love me, and I will trust your love. How would you feel towards him? Would you say to yourself, ‘Ah, now I shall have a chance to make Charley miserable? I will take away all his pleasures, and fill his life with every hard and disagreeable thing I can find. I will force him to do the hardest things. Then, I w ill give him all sorts of impossible commands.” “Oh, no, no, no!” exclaimed the indignant mother. “You know I would not. I would hug him to my heart and cover him with kisses. I would fill his life with the sweetest, best things.” “And are you more tender and more loving than God?” asked her friend. “Ah, no,” was the reply. “I see my mistake. I will not fear saying 'Your will be done,' to my Heavenly Father, any more than I'd want my Charley to fear saying it to me.”” Better and sweeter than health, or friends, or money, or fame, or ease, or prosperity, is the adorable will of our God. It brightens the dark hours with a divine halo. It sheds bright sunshine on the gloomiest paths. He always reigns who has made it his kingdom; and nothing can go amiss to him. A glorious privilege is opening before you. The first step to enter the life hidden with Christ in God is complete consecration. I cannot have you look at it as a hard and stern demand. You must do it with joy, appreciation, and enthusiasm. You must enter what I call the privilege side of consecration. I assure you, from a blessed experience, it is the happiest place you will ever find. Faith is the next thing. Faith is essential to receiving any gift. Our friends may give us something in its entirety, but we do not own it until we believe they have given it and we claim it. This is especially true for gifts that are purely mental or spiritual. Another may love us without limit. But, until we believe it, it never becomes ours. I suppose most Christians know this about their forgiveness. They know that the preaching of Jesus' forgiveness of sins might have gone on forever. But, it would never be theirs until they claimed the forgiveness. They had to believe it first. But, in living the Christian life, they lose sight of this. They think, having been saved by faith, they must now live by works. Instead of continuing to receive, they now must begin to do. This makes our declaration that the life hid with Christ in God is to be entered by faith, seem perfectly unintelligible to them. And yet it is plainly declared, that “as we have received Christ Jesus the Lord, so we are to walk in Him.” We received Him by faith, and by faith alone; so we are to walk in Him by faith, and by faith alone. Our faith in this hidden life is the same as the faith that moved us from the kingdom of darkness to God's Son. It just relies on a different thing. Then we believed that Jesus was our Saviour from sin's guilt. Our faith made it so. Now, we must believe He is our Saviour from sin's power. Our faith will make it so. We trusted Him for our justification, and it became ours. Now, we must trust Him for our sanctification, and it shall be ours, too. Then we took Him as a Saviour in the future from our sins' penalties. Now, we must take Him as a Saviour in the present from our sins' bondage. Then He was our Redeemer, now He is to be our Life. Then He lifted us from the pit. Now, He is to seat us in heavenly places with Himself. I mean this based on both experimental and practical evidence. fields.title: Difficulties Concerning Consecration
fields.body_html:
Christians must know the enemy's devices. He will oppose every step of the soul's progress. And, especially, he is busy when he sees a believer awakened to a hunger for righteousness. They seek to grasp all the fullness in the Lord Jesus Christ. One of the first difficulties he throws in their way is about consecration. The seeker after holiness receives the instruction to consecrate himself. He tries to do so. But at once he meets with a difficulty. He has done it, as he thinks. Yet, he feels no different.

Nothing seems changed, as he expected. He feels baffled and, in despair, asks, “How am I to know when I am consecrated?”

At this point, the one grand temptation is to feel. It always tries to assert itself, and it often succeeds.

The soul cannot believe it is consecrated until it experiences consecration. It cannot believe God has taken it, as it does not feel that. As usual, it puts feeling first and faith second. Now, God's rule is simple: faith first, feelings second, in all things. It's futile to try to change this.

To resist this temptation about consecration, take God's side. Put faith before feeling. Surrender yourself completely and without reservation to the Lord. Use your current understanding. Ask the Holy Spirit to reveal anything in your heart or life that is against God. If He shows you anything, give it to the Lord immediately, and say in reference to it, “Your will be done.” If He shows you nothing, then you must believe that there is nothing, and must conclude that you have given Him all. Then you must believe that He takes you. You must not wait to feel either that you have given yourself or that He has taken you. You must simply believe it, and reckon it to be the case.

If you were to give an estate to a friend, you would have to give it, and he would have to receive it by faith. No one can hand over an estate. Its gift and reception are a mental transaction, and thus, a matter of faith. If you gave an estate to a friend for one day, you might wonder if you really had, and if he took it. You might then feel the need to renew the gift the next day. If, on the third day, you still felt uncertain, you would renew it again. You would repeat this process daily for months or years.

What would your friend think? And what would your mind be like after all that?

Your friend would doubt if you meant to give it to him. You would be so confused that you wouldn't know if the estate was yours, his, or someone else's. Now, is this not how you have acted towards God in this matter of consecration? You have given yourself to Him daily for months. But, after each time, you have wondered if you truly gave yourself to Him and if He accepted you. Since you felt no different, you concluded, after much doubt, that it was not done.

Dear believer, this confusion will last forever unless you end it with faith. You must accept the matter as settled. Only then can you expect a change of feeling. The law of offerings to the Lord proves that everything given to Him becomes holy. It is set apart and cannot be used for any other purpose. To do so would be disrespect.

“Devoted things, both of man and beast, are most holy to the Lord. “They cannot sell or redeem them.

Once the Israelites gave the devoted thing to the Lord, they reckoned it as belonging to the Lord.” No one dared to reclaim it. The giver might have made his offering with reluctance and a lack of enthusiasm. But, once made, the matter was out of his hands. By God's own law, the gift became “most holy unto the Lord.””

It was not the intention of the giver that made it holy, but the holiness of the receiver. “The altar sanctifies the gift.” And an offering once laid upon the altar, from that moment belonged to the L ord.

I can imagine the one who had deposited a gift. He might then doubt his sincerity and honesty in doing so. He would return to the priest, anxious about his sincerity. I am sure the priest would have silenced him at once. He would have said, “I do not know your motives in giving your offering.”

The facts are that you did give it, and that it is the Lord’s, for every devoted thing is most holy unto Him. “It is too late to recall the transaction now.” All Israel, not just the priest, would be shocked at a man who, having offered his gift, tried to take it back. And yet, day after day, earnest Christians, who would shudder at a Jew's disrespect, are guilty of a similar act. They consecrate themselves to the Lord, then take it back through unbelief. Because God is not visibly present to the eye, it is difficult to feel that a transaction with Him is real.

If, when we consecrated ourselves, we could see Him, it would feel real. We would know we had given our word and could not take it back, no matter how much we might want to. It would have to us the binding power of a spoken promise to an earthly friend. It always has that power to a man of honor.

We need to see that God's presence is always a certain fact. Every act of our soul is done right before Him. A word spoken in prayer is as really spoken to Him, as if our eyes could see Him and our hands could touch Him.

Then, we will no longer have vague ideas about our relations with Him. We will feel the weight of every word we say in His presence. I know some will say, “Ah, yes. “But, if He would only speak to me and say that He took me when I gave myself to Him, I would then believe it.”

“No, of course you would not. But, He does not usually say this until the soul has first proved its loyalty by believing what He has already said. It is he that believes who has the witness, not he that doubted. And by His very command to us to present ourselves to Him as a living sacrifice, He has pledged Himself to receive us.

I cannot imagine an honorable man asking another to give him a thing he was doubtful about taking. I can imagine even less a loving parent acting so towards a darling child. “My son, give me your heart, and let your eyes observe my ways .” Proverbs 23:26.This is a sure warrant. It means that th e moment the heart is given, it will be taken by the One who has commanded the gift. We must, then, feel the utmost confidence. When we surrender to the Lord, as He commands, He then receives us. From that moment, we are His.

A real transaction has taken place. It cannot be violated without dishonor on our part. We know He will not violate it. In Deut. 26:17-19 shows God's way of working: “You have declared today that the LORD is your God, and that you will walk in his ways, and keep his statutes and his commandments and his rules, and will obey his voice. And the LORD has declared today that you are a people for his treasured possession, as he has promised you, and that you are to keep all his commandments, and that he will set you in praise and in fame and in honor high above all nations that he has made, and that you shall be a people holy to the LORD your God, as he promised .”

We declare the Lord our God. We will walk in His ways and keep His commandments. He declares us to be His, and we must keep all His commandments. And from that moment, He takes possession of us. This has always been His principle of working, and it continues to be so. “Every devoted thing is most holy to the Lord.” This is so plain that it admits no question. But, if you stil l doubt, let me refer you to a New Testament declaration. It approaches the subject differently, but it settles it, I think, quite definitively. It is in 1 John 5:14-15, and reads: “ And this is the confidence that we have toward him, that if we ask anything according to his will he hears us. And if we know that he hears us in whatever we ask, we know that we have the requests that we have asked of him .”

Is it according to His will that you should be fully consecrated to Him? There can be, of course, but one answer to this, for He has commanded it. Is it not also according to His will that He should work in you to will and to do of His good pleasure? This question also can have but one answer, for He has declared it to be His purpose. You know, then, that these things are according to His will. So, on God's word, you must know that He hears you. Now, you must go further. You must know that you have the petitions you desired of Him.

That you have, I say, not will have, or may have, but have now in actual possession. It is so that we “ Obtain promises” by faith. It is so that we have “access by faith” into the grace that is given us in our Lord Jesus Christ. Only by this do we know our hearts are “purified by faith.”

We can then live, stand, and walk by faith. I want to make this subject so clear and practical that no one will have further trouble with it. So, I will repeat what your soul must do to resolve your doubts about consecration.

I trust you have faith in the Lord Jesus to forgive your sins. I hope you know what it is to belong to God's family and to be an heir of God through faith in Christ. And now you feel springing up in your soul the longing to be conformed to the image of your Lord. You must fully surrender yourself to Him.

Only then may He work in you all the good pleasure of His will. You have tried to do this, but with no success. I want to help you now. Now, you must come to Him again. Surrender your whole self to His will, as completely as you can.

You must ask Him to show you any hidden rebellion by His Spirit. If he reveals nothing, believe there is none. Your surrender is complete. We must, then, consider this a settled matter. You have abandoned yourself to the Lord. From now on, you do not belong to yourself. Never listen to any suggestion to the contrary. If you wonder if you've fully surrendered, assert that you have. Do not even argue the matter.

Repel any such idea without hesitation and with firm resolve.

You meant it then, you mean it now, you have accomplished it. Your emotions may clamor against the surrender, but your will must hold firm. God looks at your purpose, not your feelings about it. So, your will is all you need to attend to. Having made a surrender, never question or recall it. Next, believe that God takes what you have surrendered. Reckon it is His. Not that it will be at some future time, but is now; and that He has begun to work in you to will, and to do, of His good pleasure. And here you must rest. You have nothing more to do. You belong to the Lord now, completely in His hands. He has taken on the care and management of you. He will, as His word says, “work in you that which is well-pleasing in His sight through Jesus Christ.”

But you must maintain a firm grip here. If you doubt your surrender, or God's acceptance of it, your faith will waver. A wavering faith will lead to a shaky experience, and He cannot work. But, while you trust He works, His work changes you. It makes you more like Christ, from glory to glory, by His mighty Spirit. Do you, now, at this moment, surrender yourself wholly to Him? You answer, yes. Then, my dear friend, reckon that you are His. He has taken you. He is working in you to will and to do of His good pleasure. And keep on reckoning this.

It will help you to put your thoughts into words. Say to yourself and to God, “Lord, I am yours. I yield myself to you, and I believe you do take me.” I leave myself with you. “Work in me all the good pleasure of thy will. I will only lie still in thy hands and trust you.” Make this a daily act of your will.

Many times a day, return to it as your constant attitude before Him. Confess it to yourself. Confess it to your God. Confess it to your friends. Always declare the Lord as your God. Commit to walking in His ways and keeping His laws.

You will then find that He has claimed you as His special people. You must keep all His commandments and be “a holy people unto the Lord, as He has spoken.”

You may find a few simple rules helpful here. I advise using them in daily devotions. They should test the soul until we gain clarity on this matter.

I. State clearly your faith in Christ as your Saviour. Also, acknowledge that you believe He has reconciled you to God, as per 2 Cor. 5:18-19 “ All this is from God, who through Christ reconciled us to himself and gave us the ministry of reconciliation; that is, in Christ God was reconciling the world to himself, not counting their trespasses against them, and entrusting to us the message of reconciliation.”

II. Definitely, acknowledge God as your Father. You are His redeemed and forgiven child, according to Galatians 4:5, “ to redeem those who were under the law, so that we might receive adoption as sons.”

III. Surrender completely to the Lord, body, soul, and spirit. Obey Him in everything where His will is known, per Romans. 12:12. “Rejoice in hope, be patient in tribulation, be constant in prayer.”

IV. Believe, against all odds, that God takes what you abandon to Him. He will work in you, unless you frustrate His grace. See 2 Corinthians. 6:17-18 “ Therefore go out from their midst, and be separate from them, says the Lord, and touch no unclean thing; then I will welcome you, and I will be a father to you, and you shall be sons and daughters to me, says the Lord Almighty .” , and Philippians. 2:13. “For it is G od who works in you, both to will and to work for his good pleasure.”

V. Don't use your feelings to test your relations with God. Focus on your will and faith instead.

And count all these steps you are now taking as settled, though the enemy may make it seem otherwise. Heb. 10:22-23. “Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, with our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.

Let us hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering, for he who promised is faithful.”

VI. Never, under any circumstances, should you doubt or feel discouraged. Remember, that all discouragement is from the devil, and refuse to admit it; according to John 14:1 “Let not your hearts be troubled. Believe in God, believe also in me ” V27 “Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. Not as the world gives do I give to you. Let not your hearts be troubled, neither let them be afraid.”

VII. Cultivate the habit of expressing your faith in clear words. Repeat often, “I am all the Lord's.

He is working in me now to will and to do of His good pleasure,” according to Heb. 13:21 “ equip you with everything good that you may do his will, working in us that which is pleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever and ever.

Amen.

And, especially, he is busy when he sees a believer awakened to a hunger for righteousness. They seek to grasp all the fullness in the Lord Jesus Christ.
