Of such a nature is kingship in this kingdom of heaven. Each soul can make the application for itself, without need of comment from me. In ( Mathew 5: 6-7), we have the King of this kingdom describing the characteristics of His kingdom and giving the laws for Hi s subjects. “Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be satisfied. “Blessed are the merciful, for they shall receive mercy. “Not the rich, or great, or wise, or learned. But the poor in spirit, the meek, the merciful, the pure in heart, those who mourn, and those who hunger and thirst. Also, the persecuted, reviled, and slandered. All such belong to this kingdom. These kings are gentle, yielding, meek, and charitable. They reign with that power. One Christian asked anoth er, “How can I make people respect me?” “I would command their respect,” was the reply. This meant, not that he should demand, “Respect me!” But, he should act, live, and be, so that all would respect him. Men can win a show of respect by being tyrannical. But, to rule their hearts, they must try other methods. Our Lord developed this thought to some who wished to share His throne. He called them to Him, and said, “But Jesus called them to him and said, “You know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it o ver them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.”(Mathew 20:25). But it shall not be so among you. Whoever wants to be great must be your minister. Whoever wants to be first must be the servant of all. For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.” From a human view, only one man reigns. He is the one who can be lord over those around him. From the divine standpoint the soul that serves is the soul that reigns. Not he who demands most, receives this inward crowning, but he who gives up most. What greater leadership can be imagined than Christ's in the Sermon on the Mount? “But I say to you, do not resist the one who is evil. But if anyone slaps you on the right cheek, turn to him the other also . ” If someone sues you and takes your shirt, give them your coat too . And if anyone forces you to go one mile, go with him two miles. (Mathew 5:39) Surely only a soul that is in harmony with God can mount such a throne of dominion as this! But this is our destiny. We are made for this purpose. We are born of a kingly race, and are heirs to this Inexpressible kingdom; “ and if children, then heirs — heirs of God and fellow heirs with Christ, provided we suffer with him in order that we may also be glorified with him .”(Romans 8:17) With that we could realize this, and, see in every act of service or surrender, an upward step. It would lead us to our kingdom and throne! I mean this in a very practical sense. I mean that our daily, humble tasks and small sacrifices, if done well, will be steps up a ladder to our thrones. If we are faithful over the “few things” of our earthly kingdom, we shall be made rulers over the “many things” of the heavenly kingdom. He who serves and suffers for Christ will reign with Him. He will be the “chiefest” in His kingdom of love. Knowing this, who would hesitate to turn the other cheek? A kingdom and a throne are to be won. Joseph was a type of all this. In slavery and in prison he reigned as king, as truly as when seated on Pharaoh’s throne or riding in Pharaoh’s chariot. (See Gen. 39:6) “So he left all that he had in Joseph’s charge, and because of him he had no concern about anything but the food he ate. Now Joseph was handsome in form and appearance.” (Genesis 39:22-23.) “ And the keeper of the prison put Joseph in charge of all the prisoners who were in the prison. Whatever was done there, he was the one who did it. The keeper of the prison paid no attention to anything that was in Joseph’s charge, beca use the LORD was with him. And whatever he did, the LORD made it succeed.” He became the greatest by being the least, the chiefest by being servant of all. Dear reader, are you ruling in this way, in this kind of kingdom? Are you the greatest in your small world — at home, church, or in your social circle? Then be the least. Be the servant of everyone. If not, your kingdom is not Christ’s kingdom, and your throne is not shared with Him. Accessing the secrets and power of this inner kingdom is not a fantasy . It’s not just an imagined victory. It’s a real and true way of reigning. It will make you rise above the world and its concerns. You will move through it, unaffected by its praise or criticism. You will live in a place of peace and victory that the world can neither give nor take away. “For the kingdom of God is not in word but in power.” It is not a talk but a fact , and those who are in it recognize their kingship and prove it by reigning. But perhaps thou will say, “How can I enter into this kingdom , if I am not already in?” Let our Lord himself answer you: “At that time the disciples came to Jesus, saying, 'Who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven? ” (Mathew 18:1) “And calling to him a child, he put him in the midst of them and said , 'Truly, I say to you, unless you turn and become like children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven. Whoever humbles himself like this child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.”(Mathew 18:2 -3) It is a kingdom of childlike hearts, and only such can en ter it. To be a “little child” means simply to be one. I cannot describe it better than this. We all know little children. We delight in their simplicity, trust, and carelessness. We admire their unquestioning obedience to authority. To be the greatest in this divine kingdom, one must have the most of this child's trusting, tender, and obedient heart. It is guileless and self-forgetting. “Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven, but the one who does the will of my Fa ther who is in heaven.”( Matthew 7:21 ) .It is not saying, but doing, that will avail us here. We must be a child, or we cannot sit on the child’s throne. And to be a child means to do the Father’s will, since the very essence of true childhood is the spirit of obedience united to the spirit of trust. Become a little child. Set aside your greatness, self-assertion, and wisdom. Give up your strength and self-dependence. Consent to die to your old self. Be born again into the kingdom of God. The only way out of one life into another is by a death to one and a new birth into the other. It is the old story, therefore, reiterated so often and in so many different ways, of through death to life. Die, then, that you my live. Lose your own life that you may find Christ’s life. They can only enter the butterfly's kingdom by dying to its caterpillar life, and then becoming a butterfly. Likewise, we can only enter God's kingdom by dying to the kingdom of self, and then rising to life in Christ. Let go of everything natural. This includes your ideas, plans, and thoughts. Instead, accept God's plans, ways, and thoughts. Do this faithfully and persistently. You shall, at last, sit on His throne and reign with Him in an eternal kingdom. It will break and consume all other kingdoms, and stand forever. There is no other way. This kingdom can't be entered through pride, appearance, or power . It can only be entered by littleness, helplessness, childlikeness, babyhood, and death. Only he who humbles himself shall be exalted. To share Christ's throne, we must first follow Him in suffering, loss, and crucifixion. If we suffer with him, we shall also reign with Him. Not as an arbitrary reward for our suffering, but as the result that will follow in the very nature of things. Christ's loss must bring Christ's gain. His death must bring His resurrection. To follow Him in the regeneration will, without fail, bring the soul that follows to His crown and throne. In a volume of sermons for children, I have found a vivid illustration of this royal kingdom: – A young boy from one of the refuges in England had risked his life to save his friend. The Queen of England had sent him a medal through one of her earls. His friends pushed him forward to receive it, as he was shy and nervous and tried to step away. Look at the honorable chairman. He had come from the House of Lords, where earls, dukes, and distinguished men like lawyers, judges, statesmen, and warriors were gathered. Royal princes were also there. Yet, all peer though he was, he was moved. He murmured, “I have the honor,” and pinned the lifesaving medal on the child's jacket. His heart was full. He paused to swallow down something that would rise in his throat before he could go on. There is the 'glory and honor' of statesmen, warriors, and lawyers. But the glory of selfless lifesaving excels all. That was the wondrous glory won by this boy.” He had plunged into the stream and shared a drowning boy's risk. That little hand, look at it there, steadying him by holding the table, had come out holding the saved. “Why has self -forgetfulness such mighty power? How was it that a twelve-year old boy could bow down an audience of grown men before him? What gave to that brow, that it’s stubby crown of carroty hair, a glory and honor more than the luster of gold and jewels? Why did that small body in its little breeches and jacket, wiping its tears on the rough little sleeve, grip thousands of hearts? Why did it make them, for a time, loyal subjects of its kingdom? Why was all this so? It was so because that little boy had been like Christ, in his spirit of selfless sacrifice for others.” He had some of the beauty we are meant to worship. It is the glory that makes angels shout. All of heaven falls and adores. They say, “ saying with a loud voice, Worthy is the Lamb who was slain, to receive power and wealth and wisdom and might and honor and glory and blessing!”( Revelations 5:12) .The Lamb that was slain is the mightiest King ever. All who share His spirit are in His kingdom. This kingdom is not a place, but a character. So, those without that character cannot be in it. We pray daily, “Your kingdom come.” Do we know what we are praying for? Do we comprehend the change it will make in us if it comes in us? Are we willing to be so changed? What is the kingdom of God but the rule of God? And what is the rule of God but the will of God? Therefore, when we pray, “Your will be done on earth as it is in heaven,” we have touched the secret of it all. A group of savages might take over a kingdom by force, but to truly control its civilization, they must follow its rules. The same is true for the kingdom of heaven. It only grants its power to those who obey its laws. “ The one who conquers, I will grant him to sit with me on my throne, as I also conquered and sat down with my Father on his throne . ”( Revelation 3:21 ) “He always reigns who sides with God,” says an old writer. And again, “He who perfectly accepts the will of God, dwells in a perpetual kingdom.” Are you reigning after this fashion and in this sort of a kingdom? Are you the most important by being the servant of all? Are you a king over your circumstances, or do your circumstances reign over you? Do you triumph over your temptations, or do your temptations triumph over you? Can you sit on an inward throne in the midst of outward defeat and loss? Can you conquer by yielding, and become the greatest by being the least? If you can’t answer yes to all these questions, then you can’t come into his kingdom. “Whatever yo ur lot or men's opinions, you are among those whom our Lord calls 'the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.'”

fields.title: The Chariots of God
fields.body_html:
“The chariots of God are twice ten thousand, thousands upon thousands; the Lord is among them; Sinai is now in the sanctuary. (Psalm 68:17.)

Chariots are for transportation and moving forward. Earthly chariots carry their riders to their destinations, overcoming all obstacles. God's chariots carry their souls. No words can express the glorious places to which that soul shall arrive who travels in the chariots of God. And our verse tells us t hey are “very many.” All around us on every side they wait for us; but we, sadly, we do not always see them. Earth’s chariots are always visible, but God’s chariots are Invisible.

“So he sent there horses and chariots and a great army, and they came by night and surrounded the city.

When the servant of the man of God rose early in the morning and went out, behold, an army with horses and chariots was all around the city. And the servant said, “Alas, my master! What shall we do?

He said, “Do not be afraid, for those who are with us are more than those who are with them. “Then Elisha prayed and said, “O Lord, please open his eyes that he may see.” So the Lord opened the eyes of the young man, and he saw, and behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.” (2 Kings 6:14 -17) This is the prayer we need to pray for ourselves and for one another, “Lord, open our eyes that we may see.” For the world all around us is full of God’s horses and chariots, waiting to carry us to plac es of glorious victory. But they do not look like chariots. They look instead like enemies, sufferings, trials, defeats, misunderstandings, disappointments, unkindnesses. They look like massive cars of misery, waiting to crush us. But they are chariots of triumph. They can take us to the heights of victory our souls long for.

If we would “ride on the high places of the earth , ” we must get into the chariots that can take us there; and only the “chariots of God” are equal to such lofty riding as this . (Deuteronomy 32:12-13) “The Lord alone guided him ; no foreign god was with him. He made him ride on the high places of the land, and he ate the produce of the field, and he suckled him with honey out of the rock, and oil out of the flinty rock.”

“Then you shall take delight in the Lord, and I will make you ride on the heights of the earth. I will feed you with the heritage of Jacob, your father, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken. (Isaiah 58:14).

We may make out of each event in our lives either a Juggernaut car to crush us, or a chariot in which to ride to heights of victory. It all depends upon how we take them; whether we lie down under our trials and let them roll over and crush us, or whether we climb up into them as into a chariot, and make them carry us triumphantly onward and upward.

“And as they still went on and talked, behold, chariots of fire and horses of fire separated the two of them. And Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven. And Elisha saw it and he cried, “My father, my father! The chariots of Israel and its horsemen! And he saw him no more. Then he took hold of his own clothes and tore them in two pieces.”(2Kings 2:11 - 12).Whenever we mount into God’s chariots , the same thing happens to us spiritually that happened to Elisha. We shall have a translation. Not into the heavens above us, as Elisha did, but into the heaven within us, which, after all, is almost a grander translation than his. We shall be carried up away from the low earthly groveling plane of life, where everything hurts and everything is unhappy, up into the “heavenly places in Christ Jesus,” where we shall ride in triumph over all below.

“And raised us with him and seated us with him in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus ,” (Ephesians 2:6). These “heavenly places” a re interior, not exterior, and the road that leads to them is also interior.

But the chariot that carries the soul over this road is generally some outward loss, or trial, or disappointment; some chastening that does not indeed seem for the present to be joyous, but grievous; but that nevertheless afterward yielded the peaceable fruits of righteousness to them that are exercised thereby.

“And have you forgotten the exhortation that addresses you as sons? My son, do not regard lightly the discipline of the Lord, nor be weary when reproved by him. For the Lord disciplines the one he loves, and chastises every son whom he receives. It is for discipline that you have to endure. God is treating you as sons. For what son is there whom his father does not discipline? If you are left without discipline, in which all have participated, then you are illegitimate children and not sons. Besides this, we have had earthly fathers who disciplined us, and we respected them. Shall we not much more be subject to the Father of spirits and live? For they disciplined us for a short time as it seemed best to them, but he disciplines us for our good, that we may share his holiness. For the moment, all discipline seems painful rather than pleasant, but later it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained by it.”( Hebrews 12:5-11).

Look upon these scoldings , no matter how grievous they may be for the present, as God’s chariots sent to carry your souls into the “high places” of spiritual achievem ent and uplifting, and you will find that they are, after all, “paved with love.”

“King Solomon made himself a carriage from the wood of Lebanon. He made its posts of silver, its back of gold, its seat of purple; its interior was inlaid with love by the daughters of Jerusalem.” (Song of Solomon 3:9-10 ). Your own individual chariot may look very unlovely. It may be a cross-grained relative or friend; it may be the result of human malice, or cruelty, or neglect; but every chariot sent by God must necessari ly be paved with love, since God is love, and God’s love is the sweetest, softest, tenderest thing to rest one’s self upon that was ever found by any soul anywhere. It is His love indeed that sends the chariot.

“Was your wrath against the rivers, O Lord ? Was your anger against the rivers, or your indignation against the sea, when you rode on your horses, on your chariot of salvation? You stripped the sheath from your bow, calling for many arrows. Selah, you split the earth with rivers. The mountains saw you and writhed; the raging waters swept on; the deep gave forth its voice; it lifted its hands on high. The sun and moon stood still in their place at the light of your arrows as they sped, at the flash of your glittering spear. You marched through the earth in fury; you threshed the nations in anger. You went out for the salvation of your people, or the salvation of your anointed. (Habakkuk.3:8-13) Here, the prophet tells us that it was God’s displeasure against the obstacles that beset the path of His people that made Him come to their rescue, riding in His “chariots of salvation.” Everything becomes a “chariot of salvation” when God rides upon it. The “clouds” that darken our skies and seem to shut out the shining of the sun of righteousness are, after all, if we only knew it, His chariots, into which we may mount with Him, and “ride prosperously” over all the darkness.

“Gird your sword on your thigh, O mighty one, in your splendor and majesty! In your majesty ride out victoriously for the cause of truth and meekness and righteousness; let your right hand teach you awesome deeds!”(Psalm 45:3 - 4). “He rode on a cherub and flew; he came swiftly on the wings of the wind.” ((Psalm 18:10). “There is none like God, O Jeshurun, who rides through the heaven s to your help, through the skies in his majesty.” (Deuteronomy 33:26). A late writer has said that we cannot, by even the most vigorous and toilsome efforts, sweep away the clouds, but we can climb so high above them as to reach the clear atmosphere overhead; and he who rides with God rides upon the heavens far above all earth-born clouds.

“O kingdoms of the earth, sing to God; sing praises to the Lord, Selah to him who rides in the heavens, the ancient heavens; behold, he sends out his voice, his mighty voice. Ascribe power to God, whose majesty is over Israel, and whose power is in the skies.”(Psalm 68:32 -34 ) . This may sound fanciful, but it is really exceedingly practical when we begin to act it out in our daily lives.

I knew a lady who had a very slow servant. She was excellent in every way and very useful. But her slowness irritated her naturally quick mistress.

The lady would get angry with the girl twenty times a day. And, twenty times, she would regret it and try to control her anger. But it was in vain. Her life was made miserable by the conflict. One day, it occurred to her that she had, for a long while, been praying for patience. Perhaps this slow servant was the very chariot the Lord had sent to carry her soul into patience. She immediately accepted it as such, and from that time used the slowness of her servant as a chariot for her soul. And the result was a victory of patience that no slowness of anybody was ever able to disturb.

At one of our conventions, I knew a sister who had to sleep in a room with two others because of the crowd. She wanted to sleep, but they wanted to talk. The first night, she was disturbed. She lay there, feeling frustrated and upset, long after the others had quieted down. She could have slept. But the next day, she heard about God’s chariots. That night, she decided to see the talking sisters as her chariots.

They would help her learn sweetness and patience. She lay there, feeling peaceful and calm. But it got very late, and they should all have been as leep. So, she quietly said, “Sisters, I’m lying here riding in a chariot.” This brought complete silence. Her chariot had carried her to victory, both inside and out.

If we choose to ride in God’s chariots, not our own, we would experience the same.

“ Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help and rely on horses, who trust in chariots because they are many and in horsemen because they are very strong, but do not look to the Holy One of Israel or consult the Lord! And yet he is wise and brings disaster; he does not call back his words, but will arise against the house of the evildoers and against the helpers of those who work iniquity. The Egyptians are man, and not God, and their horses are flesh, and not spirit. When the Lord stretches out his hand, the helper will stumble, and he who is helped will fall, and they will all perish together. (Isaiah 31:1-3) “Some trust in chariots and some in horses, but we trust in the name of the Lord our God. They collapse and fall, but we rise and stand upright. ” (Psalm. 20:7 -8). Our constant temptation is to trust in the “chariots of Egypt.” We can see them. They are real and look substantial. But, God's chariots are invisible and intangible. It's hard to believe they are there. Our eyes are not opened to see them.

“By your messengers you have mocked the Lord, and you have said, ‘with my many chariots I have gone up the heights of the mountains, to the far recesses of Lebanon; I felled its tallest cedars, its choicest cypresses; I entered its farthest lodging place, its most fruitful forest.” We try to reach the high places with the “multitude of our chariots.” We first depend on one thing, then another. We do this to improve our spirit and gain spiritual victories. We “go down to Egypt for help.” (2 Kings 19: 23).

And God is obliged often to destroy all our own chariots before he can bring us to the point of mounting into His.

“And in that day, declares the Lord, I will cut off your horses from among you and will destroy your chariots ;”( Micah 5:10). “An d to overthrow the throne of kingdoms. I am about to destroy the strength of the kingdoms of the nations, and overthrow the chariots and their riders. And the horses and their riders shall go down, everyone by the sword of his brother.” (Haggai. 2:22) .We rely too much on a dear friend to aid our spiritual growth. So, the Lord must separate us from that friend. We believe our spiritual growth relies on a favorite preacher's ministry. Now, we are mysteriously removed. We see our prayer-meeting or Bible-class as our main source of spiritual strength. Now, we are unable to attend it. And the “chariot of God,” which alone can carry us to the places where we hoped to be taken by the instrumentalities upon which we have been depending, is to be found in the very deprivations we have so mourned over. God must burn up with the fire of His love every chariot of our own that stands in the way of our mounting into His.

“For behold, the Lord will come in fire, and his chariots like the whirlwind, to render his anger in fury, and his rebuke with flames of fire.”(Isaiah. 66:15) .Let us be thankful, then, for every trial that will help to destroy our chariots, and will compel us to take refuge in the chariot of God, which stands ready and waiting beside us.

“For God alone, O my soul, wait in silence, for my hope is from him. He only is my rock and my salvation, my fortress; I shall not be shaken. On God rests my salvation and my glory; my mighty rock, my refuge is God. Trust in him at all times, O people; pour out your heart before him; God is a refuge for us. Selah.” (Psalm. 62:5 -8).We have to be brought to the place where all other refuges fail us, before we can say, He only. We say, He and something else.

“His, and my experience,” or “my church relationships,” or “my Christian work”; and all that comes after the “and” must be taken away from us, or must be proved useless, before we can come to “He only.”” As long as visible chariots are at hand, the soul will not mount into the invisible ones.

“Sing to God, si ng praises to his name; lift up a song to him who rides through the deserts; his name is the Lord; exult before him!” (Psalm. 68:4).If we want to ride with God “upon the heavens,” we have to be brought to an end of all riding upon the earth.

“Your procession is seen, O God, the procession of my God, my King, into the sanctuary.” (Psalm.

68:24). To see God’s goings, we must get into the sanctuary of his presence; and to share in His goings and go with Him, we must abandon all earthly goings.

“A man’s steps are from the Lord; how then can man understand his way?”(Proverbs.20:24). “My steps have held fast to your paths; my feet have not slipped.”(Psalm. 17:5).

“I waited patiently for the Lord; he inclined to me and heard my cry.”(Psalm.40:1). When we m ount into God’s chariot our goings are “established,” for no obstacles can hinder its triumphal course. All losses therefore are gains that bring us to this.

“But whatever gain I had, I counted as loss for the sake of Christ. Indeed, I count everything as loss because of the surpassing worth of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord. For his sake I have suffered the loss of all things and count them as rubbish, in order that I may gain Christ and be found in him, not having a righteousness of my own that comes from the law, but that which comes through faith in Christ, the righteousness from God that depends on faith.” (Philippians.3:7 -9). Paul understood this, and he gloried in the losses which brought him such unspeakable gain.

“So to keep me from becoming co nceited because of the surpassing greatness of the revelations, a thorn was given me in the flesh, a messenger of Satan to harass me, to keep me from becoming conceited. Three times I pleaded with the Lord about this, that it should leave me. But he said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.” Therefore I will boast all the more gladly of my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest upon me. For the sake of Christ, then, I am content with weaknesses, insults, hardships, persecutions, and calamities. For when I am weak, then I am strong.” (2 Corinthians.12:7 -10) Even the “thorn in the flesh,” the messenger of Satan sent to trouble him, became just a chariot for his willing heart, taking him to victories he could not have reached otherwise. To “take pleasure” in one’s struggles — what is that if not turning them into the greatest of chariots?

Joseph dreamed of his future triumphs and reign. But, to the eye of sense, the chariots that carried him there were bitter failures. It was a strange road to a kingdom. It went through slavery and a prison. Yet, there was no other way for Joseph to reach his triumph. His dream, Gen. 37:5-10 “Now Joseph had a dream, and when he told it to his brothers they hated him even more. He said to them, “Hear this dream that I have dreamed: Behold, we were binding sheaves in the field, and behold, my sheaf arose and stood upright. And behold, your sheaves gathered around it and bowed down to my sheaf.” His brothers said to him, Are you indeed to reign over us? Or are you indeed to rule over us? So they hated him even more for his dreams and for his words. Then he dreamed another dream and told it to his brothers and said, Behold, I have dreamed another dream. Behold, the sun, the moon, and eleven stars were bowing down to me. But when he told it to his father and to his brothers, his father rebuked him and said to him, what is this dream that you have dreamed? Shall I and your mother and your brothers indeed come to bow ourselves to t he ground before you?”

His chariots, Genesis. 37:19-20 “They said to one another, “Here comes this dreamer. Come now, let us kill him and throw him into one of the pits. Then we will say that a fierce animal has devoured him, and we will see what will b ecome of his dreams.” Genesis 27:28 “May God give you of the dew of heaven and of the fatness of the earth and plenty of grain and wine.” Genesis 39:19 -20 “As soon as his master heard the words that his wife spoke to him, “This is the way your servant treated me,” his anger was kindled. And Joseph’s master took him and put him into the prison, the place where the king’s prisoners were confined, and he was there in prison.” And Joseph’s master took him and put him into the prison, the place where the ki ng’s prisoners were confined, and he was there in prison; how he rode in his chariots, Genesis. 39:1-6 “Now Joseph had been brought down to Egypt, and Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, the captain of the guard, an Egyptian, had bought him from the Ishmaelites who had brought him down there. The Lord was with Joseph, and he became a successful man, and he was in the house of his Egyptian master. His master saw that the Lord was with him and that the Lord caused all that he did to succeed in his hands. So Joseph found favor in his sight and attended him, and he made him overseer of his house and put him in charge of all that he had. From the time that he made him overseer in his house and over all that he had, the Lord blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake; the blessing of the Lord was on all that he had, in house and field. So he left all that he had in Joseph’s charge, and because of him he had no concern about anything but the food he ate.”

Genesis 39:21-23 “ But the LORD was with Joseph and showed him steadfast love and gave him favor in the sight of the keeper of the prison. And the keeper of the prison put Joseph in charge of all the prisoners who were in the prison. Whatever was done there, he was the one who did it. The keeper of the prison paid no attention to anything that was in Joseph’s charge, because the LORD was with him.

And whatever he did, the LORD made it succeed .” His triumph.

And now a word as to how one is to mount into these chariots. My answer would be simply this: Find out where God is in each one of them, and hide yourself in Him. Or, in other words, do what the little child does when trouble comes, who finds its mother and hides in her arms. The real chariot, after all that, that takes us triumphantly through is the carrying of God.

Isaiah. 46:4 “Even to your old age I am he, and to gray hairs I will carry you. I have made, and I will bear; I will carry and will save.” The baby carried in the chariot of its mother’s arms rides triumphantly through the hardest places and does not even know they are hard.

Isaiah. 63: 9 “ In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them; in his love and in his pity he redeemed them; he lifted them and carried them all the days of old.”.And how much more w e, who are carried in the chariot of the “arms of God.” Get into your chariot, then. Take each thing that is wrong in your lives as God’s chariot for you. No matter who built the wrong, it is now God's chariot for you. It must carry you to a heavenly place of triumph. Shut out all the second causes, and find the Lord in it. Say, “Lord, open my eyes that I may see, not the visible enemy, but thy unseen chariots of deliverance.”

Accept His will in the trial, whatever it may be, and hide yourself in His arm s of love. Say, “Your will be done; Your will be done!” over and over.

Shut out every other thought but the one thought of submission to His will and of trust in His love.

Make your trial your chariot. Then, your soul will “ride upon the heavens” with God in a way you never dreamed possible.

I have no doubt. If our eyes were opened, we would see our homes, businesses, and streets filled with the “chariots of God.” There is no need for any of us to walk for lack of chariots.

That cross inmate of your household, who has made life a burden, may henceforth be a glorious chariot.

It will carry you to the heights of heavenly patience and longsuffering. Your misunderstanding, mortification, unkindness, disappointment, loss, and defeat are chariots. They wait to carry you to the heights of victory you have longed for.

Then, with thankful hearts, mount into them. Lose sight of all second causes in the shining of His love.

He will carry you in His arms, ensuring your safety and celebrating victory over it all.
fields.body_text: “The chariots of God are twice ten thousand, thousands upon thousands; the Lord is among them; Sinai is now in the sanctuary. (Psalm 68:17.) Chariots are for transportation and moving forward. Earthly chariots carry their riders to their destinations, overcoming all obstacles. God's chariots carry their souls. No words can express the glorious places to which that soul shall arrive who travels in the chariots of God. And our verse tells us t hey are “very many.” All around us on every side they wait for us; but we, sadly, we do not always see them. Earth’s chariots are always visible, but God’s chariots are Invisible. “So he sent there horses and chariots and a great army, and they came by night and surrounded the city. When the servant of the man of God rose early in the morning and went out, behold, an army with horses and chariots was all around the city. And the servant said, “Alas, my master! What shall we do? He said, “Do not be afraid, for those who are with us are more than those who are with them. “Then Elisha prayed and said, “O Lord, please open his eyes that he may see.” So the Lord opened the eyes of the young man, and he saw, and behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.” (2 Kings 6:14 -17) This is the prayer we need to pray for ourselves and for one another, “Lord, open our eyes that we may see.” For the world all around us is full of God’s horses and chariots, waiting to carry us to plac es of glorious victory. But they do not look like chariots. They look instead like enemies, sufferings, trials, defeats, misunderstandings, disappointments, unkindnesses. They look like massive cars of misery, waiting to crush us. But they are chariots of triumph. They can take us to the heights of victory our souls long for. If we would “ride on the high places of the earth , ” we must get into the chariots that can take us there; and only the “chariots of God” are equal to such lofty riding as this . (Deuteronomy 32:12-13) “The Lord alone guided him ; no foreign god was with him. He made him ride on the high places of the land, and he ate the produce of the field, and he suckled him with honey out of the rock, and oil out of the flinty rock.” “Then you shall take delight in the Lord, and I will make you ride on the heights of the earth. I will feed you with the heritage of Jacob, your father, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken. (Isaiah 58:14). We may make out of each event in our lives either a Juggernaut car to crush us, or a chariot in which to ride to heights of victory. It all depends upon how we take them; whether we lie down under our trials and let them roll over and crush us, or whether we climb up into them as into a chariot, and make them carry us triumphantly onward and upward. “And as they still went on and talked, behold, chariots of fire and horses of fire separated the two of them. And Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven. And Elisha saw it and he cried, “My father, my father! The chariots of Israel and its horsemen! And he saw him no more. Then he took hold of his own clothes and tore them in two pieces.”(2Kings 2:11 - 12).Whenever we mount into God’s chariots , the same thing happens to us spiritually that happened to Elisha. We shall have a translation. Not into the heavens above us, as Elisha did, but into the heaven within us, which, after all, is almost a grander translation than his. We shall be carried up away from the low earthly groveling plane of life, where everything hurts and everything is unhappy, up into the “heavenly places in Christ Jesus,” where we shall ride in triumph over all below. “And raised us with him and seated us with him in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus ,” (Ephesians 2:6). These “heavenly places” a re interior, not exterior, and the road that leads to them is also interior. But the chariot that carries the soul over this road is generally some outward loss, or trial, or disappointment; some chastening that does not indeed seem for the present to be joyous, but grievous; but that nevertheless afterward yielded the peaceable fruits of righteousness to them that are exercised thereby. “And have you forgotten the exhortation that addresses you as sons? My son, do not regard lightly the discipline of the Lord, nor be weary when reproved by him. For the Lord disciplines the one he loves, and chastises every son whom he receives. It is for discipline that you have to endure. God is treating you as sons. For what son is there whom his father does not discipline? If you are left without discipline, in which all have participated, then you are illegitimate children and not sons. Besides this, we have had earthly fathers who disciplined us, and we respected them. Shall we not much more be subject to the Father of spirits and live? For they disciplined us for a short time as it seemed best to them, but he disciplines us for our good, that we may share his holiness. For the moment, all discipline seems painful rather than pleasant, but later it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained by it.”( Hebrews 12:5-11). Look upon these scoldings , no matter how grievous they may be for the present, as God’s chariots sent to carry your souls into the “high places” of spiritual achievem ent and uplifting, and you will find that they are, after all, “paved with love.” “King Solomon made himself a carriage from the wood of Lebanon. He made its posts of silver, its back of gold, its seat of purple; its interior was inlaid with love by the daughters of Jerusalem.” (Song of Solomon 3:9-10 ). Your own individual chariot may look very unlovely. It may be a cross-grained relative or friend; it may be the result of human malice, or cruelty, or neglect; but every chariot sent by God must necessari ly be paved with love, since God is love, and God’s love is the sweetest, softest, tenderest thing to rest one’s self upon that was ever found by any soul anywhere. It is His love indeed that sends the chariot. “Was your wrath against the rivers, O Lord ? Was your anger against the rivers, or your indignation against the sea, when you rode on your horses, on your chariot of salvation? You stripped the sheath from your bow, calling for many arrows. Selah, you split the earth with rivers. The mountains saw you and writhed; the raging waters swept on; the deep gave forth its voice; it lifted its hands on high. The sun and moon stood still in their place at the light of your arrows as they sped, at the flash of your glittering spear. You marched through the earth in fury; you threshed the nations in anger. You went out for the salvation of your people, or the salvation of your anointed. (Habakkuk.3:8-13) Here, the prophet tells us that it was God’s displeasure against the obstacles that beset the path of His people that made Him come to their rescue, riding in His “chariots of salvation.” Everything becomes a “chariot of salvation” when God rides upon it. The “clouds” that darken our skies and seem to shut out the shining of the sun of righteousness are, after all, if we only knew it, His chariots, into which we may mount with Him, and “ride prosperously” over all the darkness. “Gird your sword on your thigh, O mighty one, in your splendor and majesty! In your majesty ride out victoriously for the cause of truth and meekness and righteousness; let your right hand teach you awesome deeds!”(Psalm 45:3 - 4). “He rode on a cherub and flew; he came swiftly on the wings of the wind.” ((Psalm 18:10). “There is none like God, O Jeshurun, who rides through the heaven s to your help, through the skies in his majesty.” (Deuteronomy 33:26). A late writer has said that we cannot, by even the most vigorous and toilsome efforts, sweep away the clouds, but we can climb so high above them as to reach the clear atmosphere overhead; and he who rides with God rides upon the heavens far above all earth-born clouds. “O kingdoms of the earth, sing to God; sing praises to the Lord, Selah to him who rides in the heavens, the ancient heavens; behold, he sends out his voice, his mighty voice. Ascribe power to God, whose majesty is over Israel, and whose power is in the skies.”(Psalm 68:32 -34 ) . This may sound fanciful, but it is really exceedingly practical when we begin to act it out in our daily lives. I knew a lady who had a very slow servant. She was excellent in every way and very useful. But her slowness irritated her naturally quick mistress. The lady would get angry with the girl twenty times a day. And, twenty times, she would regret it and try to control her anger. But it was in vain. Her life was made miserable by the conflict. One day, it occurred to her that she had, for a long while, been praying for patience. Perhaps this slow servant was the very chariot the Lord had sent to carry her soul into patience. She immediately accepted it as such, and from that time used the slowness of her servant as a chariot for her soul. And the result was a victory of patience that no slowness of anybody was ever able to disturb. At one of our conventions, I knew a sister who had to sleep in a room with two others because of the crowd. She wanted to sleep, but they wanted to talk. The first night, she was disturbed. She lay there, feeling frustrated and upset, long after the others had quieted down. She could have slept. But the next day, she heard about God’s chariots. That night, she decided to see the talking sisters as her chariots. They would help her learn sweetness and patience. She lay there, feeling peaceful and calm. But it got very late, and they should all have been as leep. So, she quietly said, “Sisters, I’m lying here riding in a chariot.” This brought complete silence. Her chariot had carried her to victory, both inside and out. If we choose to ride in God’s chariots, not our own, we would experience the same. “ Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help and rely on horses, who trust in chariots because they are many and in horsemen because they are very strong, but do not look to the Holy One of Israel or consult the Lord! And yet he is wise and brings disaster; he does not call back his words, but will arise against the house of the evildoers and against the helpers of those who work iniquity. The Egyptians are man, and not God, and their horses are flesh, and not spirit. When the Lord stretches out his hand, the helper will stumble, and he who is helped will fall, and they will all perish together. (Isaiah 31:1-3) “Some trust in chariots and some in horses, but we trust in the name of the Lord our God. They collapse and fall, but we rise and stand upright. ” (Psalm. 20:7 -8). Our constant temptation is to trust in the “chariots of Egypt.” We can see them. They are real and look substantial. But, God's chariots are invisible and intangible. It's hard to believe they are there. Our eyes are not opened to see them. “By your messengers you have mocked the Lord, and you have said, ‘with my many chariots I have gone up the heights of the mountains, to the far recesses of Lebanon; I felled its tallest cedars, its choicest cypresses; I entered its farthest lodging place, its most fruitful forest.” We try to reach the high places with the “multitude of our chariots.” We first depend on one thing, then another. We do this to improve our spirit and gain spiritual victories. We “go down to Egypt for help.” (2 Kings 19: 23). And God is obliged often to destroy all our own chariots before he can bring us to the point of mounting into His. “And in that day, declares the Lord, I will cut off your horses from among you and will destroy your chariots ;”( Micah 5:10). “An d to overthrow the throne of kingdoms. I am about to destroy the strength of the kingdoms of the nations, and overthrow the chariots and their riders. And the horses and their riders shall go down, everyone by the sword of his brother.” (Haggai. 2:22) .We rely too much on a dear friend to aid our spiritual growth. So, the Lord must separate us from that friend. We believe our spiritual growth relies on a favorite preacher's ministry. Now, we are mysteriously removed. We see our prayer-meeting or Bible-class as our main source of spiritual strength. Now, we are unable to attend it. And the “chariot of God,” which alone can carry us to the places where we hoped to be taken by the instrumentalities upon which we have been depending, is to be found in the very deprivations we have so mourned over. God must burn up with the fire of His love every chariot of our own that stands in the way of our mounting into His. “For behold, the Lord will come in fire, and his chariots like the whirlwind, to render his anger in fury, and his rebuke with flames of fire.”(Isaiah. 66:15) .Let us be thankful, then, for every trial that will help to destroy our chariots, and will compel us to take refuge in the chariot of God, which stands ready and waiting beside us. “For God alone, O my soul, wait in silence, for my hope is from him. He only is my rock and my salvation, my fortress; I shall not be shaken. On God rests my salvation and my glory; my mighty rock, my refuge is God. Trust in him at all times, O people; pour out your heart before him; God is a refuge for us. Selah.” (Psalm. 62:5 -8).We have to be brought to the place where all other refuges fail us, before we can say, He only. We say, He and something else. “His, and my experience,” or “my church relationships,” or “my Christian work”; and all that comes after the “and” must be taken away from us, or must be proved useless, before we can come to “He only.”” As long as visible chariots are at hand, the soul will not mount into the invisible ones. “Sing to God, si ng praises to his name; lift up a song to him who rides through the deserts; his name is the Lord; exult before him!” (Psalm. 68:4).If we want to ride with God “upon the heavens,” we have to be brought to an end of all riding upon the earth. “Your procession is seen, O God, the procession of my God, my King, into the sanctuary.” (Psalm. 68:24). To see God’s goings, we must get into the sanctuary of his presence; and to share in His goings and go with Him, we must abandon all earthly goings. “A man’s steps are from the Lord; how then can man understand his way?”(Proverbs.20:24). “My steps have held fast to your paths; my feet have not slipped.”(Psalm. 17:5). “I waited patiently for the Lord; he inclined to me and heard my cry.”(Psalm.40:1). When we m ount into God’s chariot our goings are “established,” for no obstacles can hinder its triumphal course. All losses therefore are gains that bring us to this. “But whatever gain I had, I counted as loss for the sake of Christ. Indeed, I count everything as loss because of the surpassing worth of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord. For his sake I have suffered the loss of all things and count them as rubbish, in order that I may gain Christ and be found in him, not having a righteousness of my own that comes from the law, but that which comes through faith in Christ, the righteousness from God that depends on faith.” (Philippians.3:7 -9). Paul understood this, and he gloried in the losses which brought him such unspeakable gain. “So to keep me from becoming co nceited because of the surpassing greatness of the revelations, a thorn was given me in the flesh, a messenger of Satan to harass me, to keep me from becoming conceited. Three times I pleaded with the Lord about this, that it should leave me. But he said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.” Therefore I will boast all the more gladly of my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest upon me. For the sake of Christ, then, I am content with weaknesses, insults, hardships, persecutions, and calamities. For when I am weak, then I am strong.” (2 Corinthians.12:7 -10) Even the “thorn in the flesh,” the messenger of Satan sent to trouble him, became just a chariot for his willing heart, taking him to victories he could not have reached otherwise. To “take pleasure” in one’s struggles — what is that if not turning them into the greatest of chariots? Joseph dreamed of his future triumphs and reign. But, to the eye of sense, the chariots that carried him there were bitter failures. It was a strange road to a kingdom. It went through slavery and a prison. Yet, there was no other way for Joseph to reach his triumph. His dream, Gen. 37:5-10 “Now Joseph had a dream, and when he told it to his brothers they hated him even more. He said to them, “Hear this dream that I have dreamed: Behold, we were binding sheaves in the field, and behold, my sheaf arose and stood upright. And behold, your sheaves gathered around it and bowed down to my sheaf.” His brothers said to him, Are you indeed to reign over us? Or are you indeed to rule over us? So they hated him even more for his dreams and for his words. Then he dreamed another dream and told it to his brothers and said, Behold, I have dreamed another dream. Behold, the sun, the moon, and eleven stars were bowing down to me. But when he told it to his father and to his brothers, his father rebuked him and said to him, what is this dream that you have dreamed? Shall I and your mother and your brothers indeed come to bow ourselves to t he ground before you?” His chariots, Genesis. 37:19-20 “They said to one another, “Here comes this dreamer. Come now, let us kill him and throw him into one of the pits. Then we will say that a fierce animal has devoured him, and we will see what will b ecome of his dreams.” Genesis 27:28 “May God give you of the dew of heaven and of the fatness of the earth and plenty of grain and wine.” Genesis 39:19 -20 “As soon as his master heard the words that his wife spoke to him, “This is the way your servant treated me,” his anger was kindled. And Joseph’s master took him and put him into the prison, the place where the king’s prisoners were confined, and he was there in prison.” And Joseph’s master took him and put him into the prison, the place where the ki ng’s prisoners were confined, and he was there in prison; how he rode in his chariots, Genesis. 39:1-6 “Now Joseph had been brought down to Egypt, and Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, the captain of the guard, an Egyptian, had bought him from the Ishmaelites who had brought him down there. The Lord was with Joseph, and he became a successful man, and he was in the house of his Egyptian master. His master saw that the Lord was with him and that the Lord caused all that he did to succeed in his hands. So Joseph found favor in his sight and attended him, and he made him overseer of his house and put him in charge of all that he had. From the time that he made him overseer in his house and over all that he had, the Lord blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake; the blessing of the Lord was on all that he had, in house and field. So he left all that he had in Joseph’s charge, and because of him he had no concern about anything but the food he ate.” Genesis 39:21-23 “ But the LORD was with Joseph and showed him steadfast love and gave him favor in the sight of the keeper of the prison. And the keeper of the prison put Joseph in charge of all the prisoners who were in the prison. Whatever was done there, he was the one who did it. The keeper of the prison paid no attention to anything that was in Joseph’s charge, because the LORD was with him. And whatever he did, the LORD made it succeed .” His triumph. And now a word as to how one is to mount into these chariots. My answer would be simply this: Find out where God is in each one of them, and hide yourself in Him. Or, in other words, do what the little child does when trouble comes, who finds its mother and hides in her arms. The real chariot, after all that, that takes us triumphantly through is the carrying of God. Isaiah. 46:4 “Even to your old age I am he, and to gray hairs I will carry you. I have made, and I will bear; I will carry and will save.” The baby carried in the chariot of its mother’s arms rides triumphantly through the hardest places and does not even know they are hard. Isaiah. 63: 9 “ In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them; in his love and in his pity he redeemed them; he lifted them and carried them all the days of old.”.And how much more w e, who are carried in the chariot of the “arms of God.” Get into your chariot, then. Take each thing that is wrong in your lives as God’s chariot for you. No matter who built the wrong, it is now God's chariot for you. It must carry you to a heavenly place of triumph. Shut out all the second causes, and find the Lord in it. Say, “Lord, open my eyes that I may see, not the visible enemy, but thy unseen chariots of deliverance.” Accept His will in the trial, whatever it may be, and hide yourself in His arm s of love. Say, “Your will be done; Your will be done!” over and over. Shut out every other thought but the one thought of submission to His will and of trust in His love. Make your trial your chariot. Then, your soul will “ride upon the heavens” with God in a way you never dreamed possible. I have no doubt. fields.title: Without Me You Can Do Nothing
fields.body_html:
About The Life Of Divine Union In its practical Aspects.

Not long ago, I was driving with a preacher from the Religious Society of Friends through our lovely Philadelphia Park. Our talk turned to the fruitlessness of much modern church preaching. We had, of course, discussed the lack of the Holy Ghost. But, we felt it did not explain everything. We both knew many Spirit-baptized preachers who had no fruit from their ministry. I suggested that one reason might be this.

Many ministers, when preaching or discussing religion, adopt a different tone and manner. This style removes religion from ordinary life. It fails to reach the hearts of those who live for simple pleasures and duties.

“Now, for instance,” I said. “If, in your preaching from the Friends' gallery, you could use the same tone and manner as you present one, how much more effectual and convincing your preaching would be.” “Oh, but I could not do that,” was the reply. “The preacher's gallery is so much more solemn a place than this.” “But why is it more solemn?”” I asked. “Is it not God's presence that makes the gallery and pulpit solemn? And, is it not here as well?” “Is it not just as solemn to live our daily lives as it is to preach? Should we not do the one to His glory as much as the other? I then added, as the subject opened before me, “I believe a large part of the difficulty lies in the unscriptural and unnatural divorce between our so-called religious life and our so-called temporal life. It's as if our religion were separate from us. It's a garment to put on and off as we wish.

On Sundays, and in church, we seek and worship God. So, we must show our religious life in a solemn way. But, our strained gravity and decorum deprive it of half its power. But on Mondays, we seek our own interests. So, we shed our work life and, with relief, live it. This is more natural and powerful.

The thoughts that started remained with me and gathered strength. Soon after, I attended a meeting.

The leader read John 15:5. The words, “am the vine; you are the branches. Whoever abides in me and I in him, he it is that bears much fruit, for apart from me you can do nothing,” amazed me.

I had read those words hundreds of times. I thought I understood them. But now, they seemed newly inserted in the Bible. They were ablaze with wondrous meaning.

“There it is,” I said to myself. Jesus himself said so. Apart from Him, we have no real life, whether temporal or spiritual. Therefore, all living or doing without Him is 'nothing,' as God, who sees all, calls it. Then, I wondered if anyone truly believed this. If they did, did they apply it in their daily lives? In an instant, I saw that the secret of divine union lay in its practical side as much as in any inner revelations. If I do nothing, literally nothing, apart from Christ, I am, of course, united to Him in a continual, unquestionable oneness. But if I live and work apart from Him, I have no real union, no matter how exalted my emotions about it may be.

It is to consider this aspect of the subject, therefore, that the present paper is written. I am sure that the wide divorce I spoke of, between things spiritual and things temporal, has done more than almost anything else to hinder a true union with God. It has made religion seem so outside of common life that it is almost unattainable to most people. It has made the experience of Christians stiff and unnatural. It seems to shut them out from the free, happy, childlike ease that belongs to the children of God.

I feel, therefore, that it is of vital importance for us to understand the truth of this matter. The thought that makes it clearest to me is this: our oneness with Christ contains the whole thing in a nutshell. If we are one with Him, then of course, in the very nature of things, we can do nothing without Him. For that which is one cannot act as being two. If I do anything without Christ, then I am not one with Him in that thing. Like a branch severed from the vine, I am withered and worthless. The branch should know it depends on the vine for its growth, fruit, and climbing. But it might feel it could grow and climb over a fence or around a tree. So, it might sever its connection with the vine for that part of its life.

Of course that which sought an independent life would wither and die in the very nature of things.

And just so is it with us who are branches of Christ the true vine. We can do nothing, great or small, without withering and death. The same is true for a branch of the natural vine. It will show us, at once, how fatal is the divorce I have spoken of, to the oneness with Christ, for which our souls hunger. We all know, more or less, that we cannot live our religious life without Him. But, in our so-called temporal life, who thinks our daily tasks should be done for Christ? Tasks like keeping house, doing business, making calls, darning stockings, sweeping, trimming a bonnet, or entertaining guests.

Only those who abide in Him and do them in His strength can do them rightly.

If it is Christ in the Christian leading the prayer meeting, then they are one. So, it must also be Christ in the Christian who is to keep the house and make the bargain. So, one duty is as religious as the other.

It is the man that makes the action, not the action the man.

If we “acknowledge God in all our ways,” we will make our daily life as solemn and sweet as our religious occasions. We should do everything, even eating and drinking, for His glory.

If our religion is truly our life, it must be in everything we do. No act, however human or natural, can escape its control and guidance. If God is always with us, He is with us in our business and social times as much as in our religious times. His presence is as solemn in one moment as in another.

If we for ‘In him we live and move and have our being’; as even some of your own poets have said, ‘for we are indeed his offspring “ (Acts 17:28), then we can do nothing without Him, whether we know it or not. And facts are stubborn things, thank God, and do not alter for all our feelings. In Psalm 127:1-2 ‘’unless the Lord builds the house, those who build it labor in vain. Unless the Lord watches over the city, the watchman stays awake in vain. It is in vain that you rise early and go late to rest, eating the bread of anxious toil; for he gives to his beloved sleep. ” We have a very striking illustration of this truth. The Psalmist says, “Unless the Lord builds the house, those who build it labor in vain. Unless the Lord keeps the city, the watchman wakes in vain.” It is vain for you to rise early, to sit up late, and to eat the bread of sorrows; for so He gives His beloved sleep.” The two things, done in vain unle ss the Lord is in them, are purely secular. They are simple business matters on the human plane of life. The lesson is only impressive for this: It proved God's presence in temporal things. Those were undeniable facts.

In truth, the Bible is full of this fact, and the only wonder is how any believer in the Bible could have overlooked it. God is present in all daily life, from building cities to counting hairs and noting a sparrow's fall. He is the mainspring of it all. In all we do, even eating and drinking, we must do it for Him and His glory. We are urged to live and walk in the light, so our works, both temporal and spiritual, show they are “wrought in God.”

This brings unspeakable comfort to every loving Christian heart. It turns all of life into a sacrament. It makes the kitchen, workshop, nursery, and parlor as sacred a place of service to the Lord as the prayer meeting, mission board, or charity visit.

A dear young Christian mother and housekeeper came to me, sorely grieved, because of her busy, worldly life. “There seems,” she said, “to be nothing spiritual about my life from one week’s end to the other. My large family of little children is so engrossing that I have no time for anything but attending to them and my household duties. Each night, I go to bed sick at heart. I have felt separated from my Lord all day and could do nothing for Him.” I told her what I wrote above. I assured her that all would change if she would see and acknowledge God in these homely duties. She must recognize her total dependence on Him to do them.

Her heart welcomed the good news with gladness. Months later, she told me that, from then on, life had become a transformed and glorified thing. It was now filled with the Lord's presence and the sweetness of serving Him.

Another Christian, a young lady from a fashionable family, came to me. She was in grief. Much of her life, she felt separated from God and sensed no presence of Him. I told her to avoid anything that could cause such a separation. But she assured me it was impossible. The things she meant were not wrong.

“For instance,” she said, “it is my duty to visit my mother. Yet, nothing separates me so much from God as visits” “But how would it be,” I asked, “if you visited as service to the Lord and for His glory?” “What!” she exclaimed, “visits for God? I never heard of such a thing.” “But why not?” I asked, “If it is right to make visits at all, it ought to be done for God. We are commanded to do all for His glory. If it is not right, you ought not to do it.” As a Christian,” I continued, “you must not do anything that you cannot do for Him.” “I see! I see!” she exclaimed, after a little pause, “and it makes all life look so different!

“Nothing can separate me from Him but sin. But, any act done to His glory will draw me closer and make His presence more real.”

These two instances will illustrate my meaning. I'm sure thousands of weary souls would be transformed if they realized and acted on these truths. An old spiritual writer says, to become a saint, we need not change our works. We must only aim them at God. We must do them for His glory, in His strength. Before, we did them for ourselves, with our own power. This means what our Lord meant when He said, “Without me you can do nothing.”

There is another side to this truth. It is comforting. The Psalmist develops it in the verses I quoted. “It is vain,” he says, “to rise early, to sit up late, and to eat the bread of sorrows.” Or, in other words, “What is the use of all this worry and strain? “W ork will amount to nothing unless God is in it. If he is, what folly to fret or be burdened? “His presence means He assumes care and responsibility for it all.” Ah, it is vain indeed, and I wish all of God's children knew it! We mothers ought to know it. “Our ways with our children would teach us, if we had the 'eyes to see.' How many mothers have risen early, sat up late, and eaten the bread of sorrows, just to give sleep to their beloved children?”

And how grieved their hearts would have been if, after all their pains, the children had refused to rest.

I can appeal to some mother hearts, I am sure, as thoroughly understanding my meaning. Memories will arise of the rosy boy coming in at night, tired from play. His knees were out, and his coat was torn.

We stayed up late and rose early to patch it all. We wanted the cause of all the mischief to rest undisturbed in happy childhood sleep.

How vain, and worse, would it have been for that beloved darling to have sat up late, risen early, and eaten the bread of sorrows? His mother was doing it for him just so he wouldn't have to. If this is true of mothers, it must be more so of their Maker. He came among us in bodily form to bear our burdens, carry our sorrows, and do our work, so we might “enter into His rest.”

“For whoever has entered God’s rest has also rested from his works as God did from his. ”(Hebrews 4:10). He has learned, at last, a lesson. Without Christ, he can do nothing. But, he can do all things through Christ, who strengthens him. So, he has given up all self-effort. He has abandoned himself to God to work in him to do His will. Light, heat, sound are all said to be the products of one force differently applied, and that force is motion. All things, say the scientists, can be resolved back to this. I cannot say if they are right or wrong. But, the Bible reveals a grand primal force behind motion. It is God's force. God is at the source of everything, God is the origin of everything, and God is the explanation of everything.

Without Him was not anything made that was made, and without Him is not anything done that is done.

It is no mystery. It is a simple fact. Our Lord says, “Without me you can do nothing.” Of Himself, He said, “I can do nothing on my own.” He meant that He and His Father were so one that any independent action was impossible. It must be a glorious necessity between our souls and Christ. That is why He said we could do nothing without Him. It means He has made us one with Himself. So, we cannot act independently towards Him, as He could not towards His Father.

Dear Christian, do n’t you see here a glimpse of a wonderful glory? Let’s believe that without Him, we can truly do nothing. We must believe it because it’s true. But let’s recognize this truth and start living by it from now on. Let’s turn away from living apart from Christ. From now on, let’s acknowledge Him in everything we do. Everything we do should be as a service to Him, for His glory. We rely on Him alone for wisdom, strength, patience, and everything else we need to live well.

As I said before, it is not so much a change of acts that will be necessary, as a change of motive and of dependence. The house will be kept, the children cared for, and the business run, perhaps as before.

Outwardly, it will be the same. But, inwardly, God will be acknowledged, depended on, and served.

There will be a great difference between a life of ease in His presence and a life of painful effort apart from Him.

Bringing God into our affairs will yield many benefits. We will gain divine wisdom in their conduct.

There will be a greater speed in accomplishing them. We will see a surprising increase in our resources.

We will better grasp the true nature of things. And, we will expand in ways that will amaze our cramped souls.

I mean this literally. The house will be nicer and easier to maintain. The children will learn faster. The stockings will be mended quickly. The hosts will be better at entertaining guests. The servants will be easier to manage. The deal will be more satisfying. And life will be sweeter and more peaceful. God will be i n every moment of it, and when He’s present, everything goes well. In this simple way, the soul will develop the habit of “abiding in Christ.” His presence will become the most real thing in our lives, and we will have a quiet, private connection with Him that brings us joy.

A child of God may ask, “What is the quickest way to reach the highest union with God in this life?”

There is no quicker way than the one I have been declaring. By the homely path of everyday duties done thus in God and for God, the sublimest heights are reached. Not as a reward, but as a natural result. If we abide in Him and refuse to leave Him, we shall be where He is. All that He is will be ours.

If you wish to know, dear reader, the divine union in your soul, start today to practice what I have suggested.

Offer every moment and every action of your life to God. Say to Him, “Lord, I do this in you and for your glory. You are my strength, my wisdom, and everything I need. I rely only on you.” Refuse to live even for a single moment or do anything without Him. Keep doing this until it becomes a habit for your soul. Soon, you will understand the deep desires of your soul, and they will be fulfilled in the constant presence of Christ, your life within.

Many ministers, when preaching or discussing religion, adopt a different tone and manner. This style removes religion from ordinary life. It fails to reach the hearts of those who live for simple pleasures and duties. “Now, for instance,” I said. “If, in your preaching from the Friends' gallery, you could use the same tone and manner as you present one, how much more effectual and convincing your preaching would be.” “Oh, but I could not do that,” was the reply. “The preacher's gallery is so much more solemn a place than this.” “But why is it more solemn?”” I asked. “Is it not God's presence that makes the gallery and pulpit solemn?
